Andy Burnham has doubled down on a pledge to deliver real change for people across Britain, insisting he is prepared for the challenges as the country faces severe economic headwinds.

On arriving in Liverpool on the eve of the Labour Party conference, the prime minister acknowledged both he and chancellor John Healey were working under a difficult set of circumstances in setting the autumn Budget.

Global turmoil, including wars in Iran and Ukraine, have continued to push up borrowing costs which will limit Mr Burnham’s room for manoeuvre ahead of the 28 October fiscal event.

While telling the Guardian it will be “crucial” to stabilise the public finances to put his agenda of national renewal on a good footing, Mr Burnham said he remained up to the challenge of bringing about radical change.

He was speaking as plans were unveiled to for a new help-to-buy scheme for first-time buyers. It was also announced that young people on health benefits will be offered a guaranteed job funded by the government.

Mr Burnham said: “The public would have more respect for us if we go and grab something difficult … and say, ‘right, we’re going to do something here’, rather than constantly playing the political game before fixing the problems.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham in Liverpool of the eve of his first party conference as leader ( Getty )

“It’s challenging, definitely, but there are still things that you can do. Always in politics, there are things that you can do. The question is sometimes: Are you prepared to do them? Yeah, I am prepared to do them.”

Asked about the need for a buffer against his spending plans, the so-called fiscal headroom, Mr Burnham said: “I do think it is crucial to have stability and to show that there’s a willingness to face up to the reality of some of these difficult things.

“But actually from that stability, the permission can come to make bigger change that, in the end, could put the country in a stronger position in relation to the public finances.”

As he arrived at the conference, the prime minister promised to set the UK on a new course because the decade since the Brexit vote had resulted in “drift and division”.

Mr Burnham said: “We’re going to make this a really important week where we set out a new direction for the country. We’ve had a decade since Brexit and it’s been a decade of too much drift, too much division, and we need to draw a line on that.”

He said his vision would leave “people able to have hope again that things will improve, that life will get better – and it will”.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham speaks to the media as he and his wife Marie-France Van Heel arrive for the Labour Party Conference at the ACC Liverpool ( PA )

Dressed in black jeans, T-shirt and jacket and accompanied by his wife Marie-France van Heel, Mr Burnham said it was a proud moment to attend the Labour conference for the first time as leader.

His arrival came as he also unveiled the Your First Home scheme, which will give first-time buyers the chance to buy a home with just a 2.5 per cent deposit. A loan worth 20 per cent of their property’s value will be available to help pay for the purchase as part of the scheme.

This equity loan will initially be interest-free to ensure it remains affordable.

Full details on the policy, which is similar to the Help To Buy launched in 2013, will be presented by Mr Healey at the Budget on 28 October.

Mr Burnham said: “We will step in to help more first-time buyers onto the housing ladder, especially those who can’t call on the bank of mum and dad.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham and John Healey ( PA )

“Your First Home will get them the keys to their own front door, and give builders the confidence to deliver the high-quality new homes the country needs. This Labour government is bringing back hope for people across the country.”

In another announcement on the eve of the conference, Labour revealed it was expanding its job guarantee scheme by giving young people on health benefits fast access to job opportunities in a bid to cut the welfare bill.

Through government funding, young people receiving health or disability support will be offered a guaranteed job three months after they start claiming benefits, down from 18 months.

Mr Healey is also expected to unveil a scheme aimed at encouraging foreign companies to buy more British goods and services.

The chancellor’s new UK Export Finance product, Flexible Finance, will provide loans to buyers in markets like Brazil, Morocco and Mexico, to incentivise them to purchase British products.

Meanwhile, Mr Healey, in an interview with the Sunday Times said he would “take into account” the pressure on motorists from fuel prices when asked if they were too high. Mr Healey could delay a planned 3p rise in fuel duty in January in his upcoming Budget.

On Sunday, chairman Bridget Phillipson, deputy leader Lucy Powell and deputy prime minister Louise Haigh will speak on the opening day of the party’s conference.

OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.

The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information.

Separately, AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed.

OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training “only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards” in place, adding that it expects it will have to “hit pause” again as AI develops and other issues emerge.

AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing nonpublic information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown too.

It is the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyberattack targeting AI startup Hugging Face, a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control.

In a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, President Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and coordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own.

The U.S. is not going to be “putting on brakes,” Trump told reporters outside the White House. “They want to stop our progress because we’re leading China by a lot, and we’re going to keep it that way.”

The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any nonpublic information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved.

In the Department of Education incident, OpenAI agents found API “developer keys” to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered.

In another case involving the Securities and Exchange Commission, agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do.

SEC spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said Saturday that “no nonpublic information was accessed.”

The Department of Education said earlier that it found “no evidence of any impact to our website or databases.”

Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a social media post Friday that the Hugging Face incident “is still the most severe event we’ve seen.”

OpenAI previously shared six other reports of “unexpected or concerning” behavior in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances.

More than four million homes who remain on a standard energy tariff have been urged to send in meter readings to avoid paying higher prices from October 1.

The energy price cap will rise by 4% from Thursday for a typical household in England, Scotland and Wales, just as cooler temperatures see many switching on their central heating.

The increase will see the energy bill for the average household paying by direct debit for gas and electricity reach £1,723, up £5 a month or £60 a year if this level was sustained over 12 months.

Ofgem said the increase reflected higher wholesale gas prices as a result of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, with volatile global markets remaining the dominant driver of price changes.

Comparison site Uswitch warned households without smart meters to send in readings to their supplier by the end of the month to avoid being charged higher rates for energy used before October 1.

Homes on a standard tariff with average usage are expected to spend £145 on energy in October, compared with £109 in September.

The increase of a third is down to a combination of increased usage due to cooler temperatures and higher unit rates under the latest price cap.

Ben Gallizzi, energy expert at Uswitch.com, said: “Submitting a meter reading, if you don’t have a smart meter, before or on Thursday October 1 will ensure the energy used is charged at the correct rates and not estimated by a supplier.

“That same deadline applies for the 15 million households on standard tariffs wanting to beat the hike entirely by locking in a lower-rate fixed deal before energy costs rocket for winter.”

Ofgem changes the price cap for households every three months, largely based on the cost of energy on wholesale markets.

The energy price cap was introduced by the Government in January 2019 and sets a maximum price that energy suppliers can charge consumers in England, Scotland and Wales for each kilowatt hour (kWh) of energy they use.

It does not limit total bills because householders still pay for the amount of energy they consume.

Andy Burnham has been warned that political slogans offer "no substitute" for cost-of-living support.

Dave Doogan, the SNP’s Westminster leader, stated that the Prime Minister’s promise to restore hope to the nation "rings hollow" as household bills mount.

The Labour Party conference begins on Sunday, shortly before the energy price cap rises by 4% to £1,723 a year for average households from 1 October. Mr Burnham will use the event to set out a "new direction" for the country.

The Labour leader said he was "drawing a line" under a turbulent 10 years since the Brexit vote, promising to face down left-wing pushback over his Government’s stance on the Gaza conflict.

Ahead of the conference, Mr Burnham said it was "time for Britain to believe again".

Dave Doogan wants Burnham to ‘put money in people’s pockets’ (House of Commons/PA) ( PA Media )

He added: "The message will be it’s time for Britain to believe again, it’s time for Britain to have hope again. That will be the message."

But as the event got under way, Mr Doogan called on the Prime Minister to "put money in people’s pockets".

He stated: "Andy Burnham might think he’s still in his political honeymoon but back in the real world households are preparing for another harsh winter.

"A desperate political plea to ‘hope again’ rings hollow when under the Labour Party’s watch the cost-of-living emergency goes from bad to worse.

"Andy Burnham promised ‘hope’ but all people can see and feel are even higher energy, food and petrol and diesel prices. It’s all beginning to feel very Keir Starmer. Slogans are no substitute for real help for households in a deepening cost-of-living emergency.

"Instead of more vibes and TikTok videos, people are waiting to hear how this latest UK Prime Minister is going to put money in people’s pockets."

Mr Doogan said the "permanent pattern of Westminster’s cost-of-living crisis" highlighted "the urgency of seeking to shape an economic future beyond Westminster".

He said every damaging decision from Westminster over the past two decades had made people in Scotland poorer.

He concluded: "Through a fresh start with independence, Scotland can use our vast energy resources to help households with rising prices, we can eradicate child poverty and build a wealthier, fairer Scotland as part of the European Union."

Carlos Alcaraz stepped up to flip the momentum in the Laver Cup with a crucial victory over Taylor Fritz to help Team Europe establish a 7-5 advantage after day two.

After Team World started the day session with back-to-back wins to go into the lead, it threatened to become three in a row when Fritz fought back from a set down to force two match points, but Alcaraz dug deep to prevail 6-3 4-6 13-11 in a thrilling Laver Breaker.

Alcaraz produced a masterful drop shot to help clinch a crucial two points for Team Europe in front of Roger Federer and Andy Murray at The O2 in only his second tournament since a four-month lay-off with a wrist injury.

“I’m really happy to get the win because I think it was really important. Seeing how the day was going, this is an important win and should give the team confidence,” Alcaraz said.

“I’m leaving the court really happy with everything I have done and also with the things I have been practising so far.

“I feel the drop is part of my game already. I am trying to use it in my favour. The drops made in the match, I think I won if not every drop at least a high percentage so in those moments, I try to use it because it was a good weapon for me.”

The pressure was on when Alcaraz stepped on to the black court in London after he watched Team Europe’s Alexander Zverev let slip a position of total dominance to lose to Alex De Minaur, who walked off with blood streaming from his right leg.

open image in gallery Alex De Minaur produced a brilliant comeback against Alexander Zverev (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Wire )

With the score 5-3 to Team World after the day session on Saturday, Alcaraz wrestled the initiative to take the first set, but Fritz responded and a fifth consecutive tie-break was required.

A wonderful serve-and-volley set up the first of three match points for Alcaraz, but Fritz went clutch and then fashioned two of his own – only for the seven-time major champion to stay in the match with an ace.

The O2 crowd were on their feet again after Alcaraz sent down a booming forehand winner before an outrageous drop shot could only be returned into the net by Fritz to give a vital win for Yannick Noah’s Team Europe.

It was backed up by Zverev being able to atone for his defeat to De Minaur after he formed a successful doubles’ partnership with Casper Ruud to beat Team World pair Brandon Nakashima and Alexander Bublik.

Zverev and Ruud triumphed 6-4 7-6 (7) to keep Team Europe in front ahead of Sunday’s final day.

Team World captain Andre Agassi had watched his gamble pay off at the start of Saturday, with debutant Learner Tien put in against French Open runner-up Flavio Cobolli and he was able to battle to a 6-3 2-6 10-7 win.

It earned Tien a chest bump off Agassi before De Minaur pulled off an incredible rescue act against two-time major winner Zverev.

open image in gallery Team World captain Andre Agassi, left, reacts with Learner Tien (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Wire )

Zverev raced through the first set and opened up a break in the second to serve for the match at 5-4, but De Minaur broke and survived match point in the Laver Breaker before he outlasted the German in a dramatic final rally to win 2-6 7-6 (5) 11-9

“What a place to play some tennis. This is special. Thank you guys. If you notice, my blood is red as well,” De Minaur said, with reference to Team World’s red outfit.

However, Alcaraz turned it around for Team Europe and avoided the prospect of back-to-back singles’ defeats for the first time in 18 months to gain revenge on Fritz for his loss in the 2025 edition and set up a tantalising final day.

Several British adventurers, including Ben Fogle and Bear Grylls, have rallied around Sir Ranulph Fiennes amid concerns over his care.

A care home owner in Wales, where the 82-year-old explorer had been placed for seven weeks this year, told The Telegraph they had reported several concerns about Sir Ranulph’s wellbeing to the authorities, including the police.

The same newspaper claimed to have seen an email sent by a care watchdog that reportedly said Sir Ranulph was being unlawfully kept in care homes and unable to consent to his care or treatment.

TV presenter and adventurer Mr Fogle said he was “deeply disturbed” by the reports about Sir Ranulph’s care and urged an investigation.

He wrote on social media: “That such a great man, hero of mine and a national treasure, should be treated in this way, isolated and kept away from family and friends, is very troubling. It is time for the Office for the Public Guardian and the police to investigate this case.”

A GoFundMe page has been set up to find the explorer by his stepson, Alexander Millington-Cotes, and has so far raised more than £6,600. He told The Telegraph: “I just want to be able to see him.... this just seems like a really bad dream.”

Mr Grylls also joined calls for police and the OPG to investigate, saying he and others had been “desperately trying to connect with Ran for a year now to no avail”.

open image in gallery Bear Grylls said he had failed to get in contact with Sir Ranulph for over a year ( @BearGrylls/X )

He said: “Ran is a true British icon for so many around the world – a pioneer, a humble warrior and a good friend to so many of us. He never failed to support me when I needed help. Now is our time.

“These reports of his isolation from his loved ones and treatment in care homes are so deeply disturbing. That a hero like Ran should have to face this is very hard to read. It’s past time for the Office for the Public Guardian and the police to investigate urgently. We owe it to him. Ran we are coming!”

open image in gallery Monty Don said an investigation into Sir Ranulph’s care was ‘vital’ ( PA )

BBC Gardeners’ World presenter Monty Don said: “My family and I have known Ran for over 40 years and he is one of the most inspirational, remarkable – and kindest – of men I have known. And of course, other than personal affection, he should be enjoying the admiration and respect of the whole country after such a remarkable life and not kept hidden away from family and friends.

“If anyone can be called a national treasure it is Ran and I do feel that it is vital that the OPG urgently investigates his case and all the facts can be brought to light.”

Gini Bowring, whose father Anton Bowring is Sir Ranulph’s business partner and long-standing friend, said: “Through all your expeditions and adventures, even in the most inhospitable places on Earth, we knew where you were,” according to The Telegraph.

“We knew how you were. If you needed help, we knew how to reach you. For two years, there has been silence. One minute you were there, the next…gone, unreachable!

“We don’t know where you are or how you are. We have tried to find you, and are still trying. We’re all hoping that the place where you should be safest has not become the hardest place you have ever had to face.”

open image in gallery The Care Inspectorate of Wales reportedly said Sir Ranulph was being ‘unlawfully deprived of his liberty’ ( Getty )

A spokesperson for the Care Inspectorate of Wales, which The Telegraph reported declared in an email to the Welsh care home owner that Sir Ranulph was being “unlawfully deprived of his liberty”, said: “Care Inspectorate Wales is committed to promoting the safety, wellbeing and rights of people who receive social care services across Wales.

“As part of this role, CIW monitors Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) to help ensure people living in care homes are protected and any restrictions placed on their freedom are lawful, necessary and in their best interests.

“Where a person is under continuous supervision and control, is not free to leave, and lacks the capacity to consent to their care arrangements, providers must apply to the local authority for a DoLS authorisation and notify CIW when an application has been made.

“It would not be appropriate for us to comment on an individual's personal circumstances or care arrangements.”

News.title: Fun, yes – but when will Tuchel fix this England defence?
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal
News.content:
Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

Sports.title: From Arsenal freeze & World Cup snub to future of England midfield… Lewis-Skelly proves huge point to Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Next

IT has been a hell of a four months for Myles Lewis-Skelly – and he did not even go to the World Cup.

The Arsenal star only made his first start in midfield in the Premier League for his boyhood club in May.



Fast forward to Saturday night and the 20-year-old was starting in the middle of the park for his country against the world champions.

With club-mate Declan Rice pulling out of the squad due to fitness, Lewis-Skelly was given the nod over Alex Scott to start alongside Elliot Anderson.



He made a nervy start against the mighty Spain, but who didn’t in the England side?

After that, though, like the rest of the team, he grew into the game and did not look out of place at all against the best international outfit on the planet.



It marks a stunning turnaround for the Londoner who was out of the picture under Mikel Arteta for much of the last season.

Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie were preferred to the then-teenager at left-back, while a start in his natural role of central midfield looked a world away.

A summer sale seemed a genuine possibility when he was frozen out mid-season.

But with Martin Zubimendi running on fumes as Arsenal looked to close out their first title in 22 years, Lewis-Skelly was brought back in from the cold.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He had been training in midfield for a few months, having been a No6 and a No8 in the Gunners’ academy, and started there in a 3-0 home win over Fulham on May 2.

Since then, he has not looked back.

Lewis-Skelly was superb in the Champions League semi-final victory over Atletico Madrid and impressed in the final too, which Paris Saint-Germain won on penalties.

It came a little too late to make the plane for the World Cup but Thomas Tuchel has always liked the youngster.

Playing at left-back, Lewis-Skelly scored the first goal of the Tuchel era in a 2-0 win over Albania in March 2025.



So it was no surprise to see the German bring the versatile midfielder straight back into his squad after his electric start to the Premier League season.

Zubimendi has had to get used to watching on from the bench as Lewis-Skelly struts his stuff in midfield.

And the Spaniard did again here as he was named among the substitutes for Luis de la Fuente’s reigning Euros and World Cup winners.



Lewis-Skelly’s first major contribution was a jittery pass straight to Marc Cucurella who drove into the box and saw an effort deflected out for a corner.

It was not the Arsenal man’s finest moment but was in keeping with a number of first-half errors from England involving Elliot Anderson, Jarell Quansah and, of course, Marc Guehi, who was terribly at fault for Lamine Yamal’s opener.

Lewis-Skelly shook off the early gaffe and started to assert his authority in midfield, telling team-mates where he wanted the ball and taking it in difficult positions.

He would drop back between the two centre-halves at times, to create a back three, and when Spain had goal-kicks, push forward to man-mark Rodri.

His standout moment in the first half was a drive forward, shrugging off 2024 Ballon D’Or winner Rodri and haring into the box, where he was correctly denied a penalty when going down under Pau Cubarsi pressure.



But Lewis-Skelly did look like he did not know what to do when Ballon D’Or contender for this year, Yamal, ran at him outside the box just before the break.

After the interval, MLS grew in confidence further, taking down one high ball with some tip-top chest control and almost grabbing an assist when playing through Bukayo Saka, who was denied by a last-gasp tackle.

His eyes lit up just before coming off for James Garner as he tried his luck from outside the box, but it was right down Unai Simon’s throat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Playing Spain and their stellar, tiki-taka midfield is about as tough a test as it gets.

This was not an A+ performance but Lewis-Skelly did more than enough to pass the exam.

Sports.title: Major update in probe into £300k jewellery heist at Harry Redknapp’s £5million mansion
Sports.content:
Next

A PROBE into a £300,000 jewellery heist at Harry Redknapp’s £5million mansion has ended, with no arrests.

The ex-Premier League boss’s home was targeted by a gang while the 79-year-old was visiting wife Sandra in hospital.



It was for sale at the time and one ­theory is the gang noted details on the Rightmove listing for the property, near Dorset beach resort Sandbanks.

Items taken included a £55,000 diamond heart-shaped pendant and a £42,000 Cartier bracelet.



But detectives have now ended the investigation into the burglary, in July last year, with no arrests being made.

A spokesperson for Dorset Police said: “Our investigation has concluded.



“However, should any new lines of enquiry emerge they will be investigated accordingly.”

Redknapp managed at Soccer Aid earlier this year, and also appeared on I’m A Celebrity.

He also offered to take over as Tottenham manager at the end of last season.

Last week The Sun on Sunday revealed cops had ended an investigation into a burglary at the home Ruben Dias shared with Maya Jama.

Sports.title: ‘Turned him into traffic cone’ – Fans stunned as Dani Olmo ‘cooks’ Elliot Anderson with simple skill in England vs Spain
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY’S £116million signing Elliot Anderson was left red-faced during England’s dramatic loss to Spain in the Nations League BY Dani Olmo.

The world champions came from behind – after surrendering their lead – to pick up a 3-2 win over the Three Lions in a rematch of their Euro 2024 final at Wembley.



The European champions dominated the first few minutes in London after Lamine Yamal took advantage of Marc Guehi’s disastrous error at the back and opened the scoring just two minutes after kick-off.

The Furia Roja’s dominance was illustrated by a brilliant run from Olmo, 28, just after the 20th minute when he led a dangerous counter-attack.



And in doing so, the Barcelona star flicked the ball past Anderson, 23, who was left frozen after that simple piece of skill while his opponent sprinted towards the hosts’ half.

England fans were left gobsmacked as they watched the playmaker run past the Man City midfielder like he wasn’t even there.

One supporter tweeted: “Olmo puts on a Spain shirt and suddenly has the burst and drive to turn Elliott Anderson into a traffic cone. what an odd player!”

Another commented: “DANI OLMO JUST ENDED ELLIOT ANDERSON HERE!”

A third wrote: “Olmo just sent Elliot Anderson to Manchester.”

This fan said: “He sucked the soul out of Anderson.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That one added: “Dani Olmo finished Anderson.”

And a comment read: “He just made Anderson look foolish.”

Olmo proved to be pivotal for Spain, who saw second-half subs Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal sealing an impressive win following goals by Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane that cancelled out Yamal’s opener.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll reveals he’s been inundated with support from male sex assault victims after opening up about his ordeal
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALLER Andy Carroll says he has been inundated with messages of support from male sex assault victims after telling of his own ordeal.

The former England striker, 37, said many had been in touch about their own experiences since he revealed his torment in autobiography Owning It.



And he looked relaxed yesterday as he arrived to play for non-league Dagenham & Redbridge, a club he co-owns, in a 1-0 win over Hampton & Richmond Borough.

In his book, ex-Premier League star Carroll said he was sexually assaulted while sleeping in 2021 during his second stint with Newcastle United by a “celebrity mate”, a friend of his former partner who was away at the time.



The man was convicted at what Carroll described as “humiliating and horrendous trial”.

He was jailed for three years, put on the sex offender register and banned from the village Carroll lives in.



As a sexual assault victim, Carroll had automatic anonymity and only decided to detail the incident in his book “at the last minute” after chats with present girlfriend Lou Teasdale, 42.

He wrote online: “It’s been incredibly hard for me to speak about what happened. I’m still navigating what I feel comfortable sharing publicly.

“Since speaking out, so many men have messaged me about their own experiences.

“That has been incredibly powerful and has reminded me just how important it is that men feel able to talk when they’re ready.”



The book describes how Carroll’s attacker invited himself into his home to watch a boxing match.

He said he went to bed after feeling light-headed and was woken by the visitor sexually assaulting him.

Carroll ordered the man to leave and when he tried to come back in he hit him, knocking him out.



He said: “What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I’d think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football.

“The trauma of what happened to me hasn’t gone away.”

He added: “Scary to talk about but it’s made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff.

“And if me talking about it helps just one ­person, then good. It will have been worth it.”

Sports.title: England player ratings: Bellingham bosses midfield as Gordon shows his worth to Tuchel but Guehi unsteady & gifts goal
Sports.content:
Next

MAYBE we wouldn’t have beaten them in the World Cup final after all…

Spain capitalised on England’s shoddy defence to come back from 2-1 down after Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane had got the Three Lions into the lead with a comeback of our own.



Lamine Yamal opened the scoring, with the third fastest goal that the Three Lions have ever conceded at Wembley, inside one minute with Marc Guehi caught napping on the ball.

Some Anthony Gordon magic saw the LaLiga boys set this game alight, before Harry Kane scored England’s second in four minutes to see the hosts go ahead. Unfortunately though it was downhill from there…





Kane embraced his inner John Terry and slipped on the penalty spot, watching his effort crash against the crossbar from 12 yards out, before Alex Baena and old enemy Mikel Oyarzabal added two Spanish goals to slay the Three Lions.

This is how SunSport’s England reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the Three Lions:

JAMES TRAFFORD – 5

His passing out from the back was good, but his shot stopping left something to be desired as he conceded three goals and only made two saves.

Jordan Pickford’s time between the sticks might not be over just yet, but Trafford does still show plenty of promise to be England’s future number one.



JARELL QUANSAH – 5

Came incredibly close to finding England a third goal but his headed effort was just over the bar early on in the second half.

He then lashed a shot at the face of Marc Cucurella, which the home fans enjoyed, but would’ve preferred if he found the back of the net. Defensively he was fine, but not troubled as much as Nico O’Reilly on the other side.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

EZRI KONSA – 4

He didn’t really seem very involved defensively for most of the game, so it’s hard to judge him in that sense.

He made less defensive contributions than any other England defender, but also didn’t make a huge mistake like Marc Guehi next to him.



MARC GUEHI – 3

An awful mistake early on saw him give possession away to Lamine Yamal, who made no mistake in beating James Trafford from close range to score the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium.

Was booked in the second half and struggled generally tonight throughout – a good defender who had a poor game. Perhaps a potential relegation is playing on his mind….

NICO O’REILLY – 6

Had one of, if not the toughest tasks of the night in defending against Lamine Yamal, but did so reasonably well.



Yamal, of course, was always a threat but O’Reilly made his danger known too with a beautifully stood-up cross that Harry Kane headed home to give England the lead.

His poor pass backwards was straight into the feet of Dani Olmo, who set up Alex Baena for Spain to make it 2-2.

ELLIOT ANDERSON – 6

Not at his sharpest in the first half, and almost gave Spain a second goal but for the intermittent finishing ability of Ferran Torres.

But to give him some credit he was one of the few players always looking to play the ball forwards.

He was vital in England getting level, capitalising on a Nico Williams slip to slide the ball into Anthony Gordon, and improved tenfold after that.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 6

It’s a credit to him that he didn’t look out of place against one of the best midfields in world football.

The youngster was smooth on the ball in midfield and found some good forward passes with Elliot Anderson next to him breaking up play.

His versaility also worked really nicely for England as he could slot into the left-back role when Nico O’Reilly ventured forwards.

BUKAYO SAKA – 5

Bukayo Saka vs Marc Cucurella is always a great matchup, and you never know who is going to come out on top between them.

It was an even one in this game, with both of them keeping the other fairly quiet aside from a few clever Saka moments with the ball. Nonetheless, the was the quietest attacker in the England side.



JUDE BELLINGHAM – 8

Showed top-level composure in the middle of the park to provide a perfectly-weighted through ball to Anthony Gordon for his equaliser, and won a penalty that should’ve seen England bag a third.

He was tenacious as ever in the middle of the pitch, did his defensive duties well and is a real leader – his second half really showed how technically brilliant he is too. I can’t believe there was ever a debate about him being in the side.

ANTHONY GORDON – 8

Absolutely brilliant.



His performance overall was as sharp and decisive as the imaginary sniper celebration that followed his equalizing goal.

That goal was a special one, with a neat flick into Bellingham starting it, and a composed finish to end it – he looks extremely confident and was always looking to make something happen with his electric pace on the wing.

HARRY KANE – 7

If this game was the battle for the Ballon d’Or between Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane then the latter still deserves to win it on October 26.



It was exactly what we’ve come to expect from the England No9 – a crucial goal, with good hold-up play and the ability to drop deep and create too.

He unfortunately slipped on the Wembley turf to see a penalty crash off of the crossbar in the second half, but was still very good overall.

SUBS:

MORGAN ROGERS (ANTHONY GORDON, 70) – 5

Struggled to get involved on the left side as much as Anthony Gordon did, with Spain in the ascendancy when he came on.

JAMES GARNER (MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY, 70) – 5

Not as progressive as Myles Lewis-Skelly before him, but turned possession over nicely.

DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN (HARRY KANE, 82) – N/A

Hardly involved after being introduced late as England looked for a leveller.

Hardly involved after being introduced late as England looked for a leveller.

Sports.title: England 2 Spain 3: Guehi howler & Kane penalty miss come back to haunt Three Lions as ruthless world champs win opener
Sports.content:
Next

THOMAS TUCHEL accepts he must now “embrace the chaos” as England manager. And here was the compelling proof why he has absolutely no choice.

Against the world champions, the Three Lions were disorganised defensively but full of pace and purpose in attack.



Ultimately, it was not good enough. Not against the very best.

The match-winner was substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who has a bit of history with England as he was the man who grabbed the clincher in the Euro 2024 final.



So after another breathless England display, which had fans tearing their hair out and cheering with delight in equal measure, it feels as though this country is far, far away as they have ever been from winning a major tournament.

Lamine Yamal scored the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium, in the second minute.



England should have been 4-0 down, maybe even 5-0, before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both struck and it was ludicrous that England led 2-1 at half-time.

Kane missed from the penalty spot, slipping like he did in the 2022 World Cup quarter-final against France.

Sub Alex Baena then levelled before Oyarzabal took advantage of yet more rubbish England defending.

This was the youngest team Tuchel has fielded, average age 25 years and six days, but that is no excuse for such basic errors.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This was a typical Premier League-style performance from England and there lies the problem.

The team might have courage and spirit but it cannot keep possession or avoid kamikaze defending.

The last time England were involved in a game quite so mad was the previous match, the 6-4 win over France in the World Cup third-place play-off.

This Nations League game clearly was more important for England but Spain still won and deservedly so. It could have been embarrassing.



So even had Tuchel’s team not blown it against Argentina in the semi-final, an appearance in the final against this fabulous Spanish team would have been messy.

Manchester City’s Marc Guehi, Elliot Anderson and Nico O’Reilly were all guilty of making some really bad errors at the back and anyone would think someone was bothering them.

They were not the only culprits, however.



Forget the fact that England qualified for the World Cup without conceding a goal, the defence is nowhere near as good as some think.

England conceded eight times even before playing France in Miami underlined that there are issues that manager Tuchel has to solve, going into Euro 2028.

Jordan Pickford did not always cover himself in glory in the summer and this is surely the reason why Tuchel has given James Trafford a two-game trial.

This was Trafford’s third senior appearance and he will also face the Czech Republic on Tuesday before Pickford picks up cap no 92 against Croatia next Saturday.



Yet although he made one crucial save, Trafford was repeatedly left exposed by his team-mates in that extraordinary first half

Yamal scored after just 106 seconds via the post after he picked the pocket of Guehi who was caught dithering.

World Cup final hero Ferran Torres thought he had scored but was offside and was then left unmarked after receiving a pass from Yamal but Trafford delivered a good block.

Embarrassingly, in almost a repeat move although Rodri delivered the pass, Torres was through but slipped the ball past Trafford but wide.

And Dani Olmo also fired wide after a sensational flick from Yamal although a minute later, it was the boy wonder’s Barcelona team-mate Gordon who levelled.



Nico Williams lost the ball to Anderson, Jude Bellingham drove forward and released Gordon who took one touch before dispatching the ball underneath Unai Simon.

Although Kane made a mess of one chance by getting the ball stuck under his feet before curling a shot wide, he grabbed goal no 86 for England a few seconds later.

He needed some help from Cucurella, who diverted a stooping header into the net with his thigh following a clever cross from O’Reilly.



It should have been 3-1 after England were awarded a penalty after VAR spotted Rodri’s foul on Jude Bellingham but Kane ended up slamming his spot-kick against the bar.

Yet at no stage did England ever look like to stop Spain from scoring again. O’Reilly gave the ball away again and five minutes after arriving as a sub, Baena curled a shot past Trafford.

Baena then turned provider and found Oyarzabal who, completely unmarked, dinked the ball over the advancing Trafford.

England could have made it 3-3 and Bellingham forced a good save from Simon at the end.

So, after heartbreak at the World Cup, England failed to bring any sort of feel-good factor back to the country.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tuchel certainly made mistakes against Argentina but ultimately, it was not just his fault, like it was not always Gareth Southgate’s.

When it really matters, England are still not good enough.

Sports.title: ‘Cheer of the night’ – Wembley erupts as Marc Cucurella blocks thunderous shot with his FACE in England vs Spain
Sports.content:
Next

MARC CUCURELLA taking a thunderous shot to the face during England’s Nations League defeat to Spain got “the cheer of the night” at Wembley.

The Real Madrid star spent five years in the Premier League during his time at Brighton and Chelsea.



He switched the Blues for the Bernabeu this summer in a £51million deal, which will have riled up a handful of Chelsea supporters.

And it’s clear he might have ruffled feathers among other supporters during his time in English football as he was given a hostile reception on his return.



Some fans noticed how Cucurella taking a powerful hit to the face from a Jarrell Quansah effort brought some cheers among the Wembley crowd.

One wrote on X: “Cucurella getting wiped out got best cheer of the night, unsurprisingly…”



Another added: “That cheer when Cucurella got hit in the face.”

A third joked: “Whole house cheered when Cucurella took that shot to the face.”

And a fourth said: “The cheer after Cucurella taking the ball to the face, I love my country.”

Cucurella played the full 90 minutes of Spain’s 3-2 win over Thomas Tuchel’s men.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It wasn’t the best night individually for Cucurella as he also allowed Harry Kane‘s header to bounce into the net off his knee as England went 2-1 up.

He did go close to scoring himself as a chipped effort cannoned off the foot of the post.

His Spain side quickly took the lead at Wembley as Lamine Yamal pounced on Marc Guehi’s poor mistake.



Anthony Gordon calmly levelled the score after being put clean through on goal.

And Spain went ahead for the second time thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal cool lofted finish.

Sports.title: My Tottenham were cheated out of Champions League by Man City.. but it would be madness to go back and mess with results
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY’S guilty verdict handed down on almost all of their Premier League charges is a staggering moment for football.

It is a huge task to try and wrap your head around just how far this could reach through the sport — all the people who could be impacted.



There are so many who will feel they have a claim to have some wrongs righted should City fail in their appeal and I am one of them.

During the period City’s charges cover, I was in charge of Spurs and locking horns with them for the Champions League spots over a long run.



In back-to-back seasons, 2010/11 and 2011/12, we finished one place off qualification.

The second time around, when City won the title with that Sergio Aguero goal on the final day, we finished fourth but STILL missed out as Chelsea won the Champions League to take our spot.



In May 2011, a 1-0 loss to Roberto Mancini’s side saw them qualify for Europe’s biggest competition for the first time and ended our dream of getting in there ourselves.

Who knows what would have happened if those at the Etihad had been playing by the rules like everyone else?

No one can say for sure but Tottenham fans will not be alone in feeling that they were, in some way, cheated across those seasons.

Champions League football over those two years could have changed so much for Spurs but I have no interest in the Premier League going back and deducting points from those seasons or deducting titles from City.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This whole process has been one almighty, drawn-out mess, but we are still a long way off from it being finished.

Just imagine the can of worms we would be opening if the suits were to start going back and altering league tables which have long been finalised.

Where do you start and where do you draw the line?



Not only are the clubs at the top impacted by titles, Champions League places and huge revenue missed out on — but those at the bottom will all have claims too.

Clubs who lost to City over the season and were relegated by the odd few points will start arguing their case if other results or points tallies are retrospectively changed.

Even though they have won a huge victory, the whole process has been damaging for the Premier League.

But opening up all those previous seasons would do incredible damage to a league which is the envy of the world.

City obviously need to be punished, to be made an example of, but it makes much more sense for everyone involved if those penalties cover the years to come.



I was always so proud of how, at Tottenham, we managed to compete by taking a different path to those with unlimited funds.

It was not just their incredible spending we had to deal with back then, but also that of Roman Abramovich at Chelsea.

We were up there fighting with the best of them but with a very different budget.

Rather than getting where we were because someone walked into my office with a huge sack of cash, we were working hard on the training ground.



I know of so many clubs who were battling with City to sign players but were blown out of the water by the wages they could offer.

We, and many other clubs, simply could not compete on that front.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

I signed Emmanuel Adebayor from them but he was probably on about a third of what he was earning in Manchester.

They should be hit hard when all is said and done but, as wronged as we all might feel by what happened, it would be madness to go back and start messing with results from the past.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel brutally shuts down England question live on ITV with blunt answer
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel brutally shuts down England question live on ITV with blunt answer

England suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to Spain in the Nations League at Wembley on Saturday evening, with Thomas Tuchel somewhat reserved in his reflection in the aftermath

View Image Thomas Tuchel disagreed with the assessment from a reporter (Image: ITV)

Thomas Tuchel ruthlessly shut down a reporter with a blunt answer on Anthony Gordon's goal after England's 3-2 Nations League loss to Spain on Saturday. A night to remember quickly turned into an outing to forget as the Three Lions walked away from their opening game of the competition empty-handed.

‌



Marc Guehi found himself pickpocketed by Lamine Yamal on the edge of his own area just two minutes into the match, with the Ballon d'Or nominee slotting past James Trafford from close range. Gordon levelled matters with around 10 minutes remaining of the first-half with a swift counter-attack, before Harry Kane gave the Three Lions the lead moments later after his header deflected off the thigh of Marc Cucurella and past Joan Garcia.

‌



Kane had the chance to make it 3-1 just after the break from the penalty spot, only to slip on the hallowed turf of Wembley, double striking the ball and giving away a free-kick to Spain. Goals from Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal flipped the scoreline once more, as the world champions took all three points in the capital.

‌



England come out on wrong side of Spain thriller but Thomas Tuchel gets fans back onside READ MORE :

Tuchel spoke live on ITV in the aftermath of the clash, where he was probed on his thoughts regarding England's overall performance. The line of questioning then turned to Gordon's goal potentially encapsulating the England template to success, but the head coach was quick to shut down that suggestion.

He said: "No, the Anthony Gordon goal was a counter-attack," with a wry smile, adding: "The ball went in...a counter-attack."

When questioned further, Tuchel added: "If you want to call it that, it's a ball win and a top transition goal. We scored amazing goals and could have created more if we are more clinical in the 20 metres, because we had an incredible amount of ball wins.

‌



"So, the effort against the ball is also identity. The effort against the ball, and the bravery and the courage to have the high ball wins was outstanding. I think we had 12 or 15 more ball wins in the opponents' half than Spain, but we couldn't convert enough into chances and goals, because otherwise, we would have won the match."

"Probably similar again today. We had a lot of good moments though. I think that period (where England took the lead) was as good as we've played in a long, long time, and that's the standard that we know we can reach.

Sports.title: England come out on wrong side of Spain thriller but Thomas Tuchel gets fans back onside
Sports.content:
It was great fun while it lasted. But probably summed up England. So near and yet so far.

They were undone by world champions Spain in a five-goal thriller at Wembley in what turned out to be a case of another missed opportunity. Thomas Tuchel’s nearly men were 2-1 up when Harry Kane smashed a penalty against the crossbar and with it the chance to put the game out of sight. If there was one player you would bank on to score, it would be Kane. Sadly, Spain came back and turned this brilliant rollercoaster game on its head again.

Spain ended up victorious because they have just a little bit more quality than England despite a battling, gritty and entertaining performance from Tuchel’s men.

It was not the victory which Tuchel wanted to kickstart England’s Nations League campaign but it was still enough to get the Wembley crowd back onside after the World Cup. You could not help but be entertained and yet it did again highlight the gap between the world and European champions and Tuchel’s brave battlers.

‌



It was a nightmare start for England. Nico O’Reilly passed the ball to Manchester City teammate Marc Guehi who was guilty of a shocking mistake completely out of character.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Blimey, City might be facing the possibility of relegation after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules but they are not playing in League Two just yet.

‌



Guehi turned into trouble, clearly did not see Lamine Yamal behind him and just ran the ball straight into the Spain teenager’s path. Yamal raced free, fired the ball past England keeper James Trafford and it went in off the far post to give the world champions the lead inside two minutes.

It was also an unhappy introduction for Leeds keeper James Trafford as this was his big audition and a chance to show Thomas Tuchel what he can do. Tuchel is giving Trafford and Jordan Pickford two games each in these four Nations League games.

England’s sloppiness continued. Myles Lewis-Skelly’s pass across his own box - unforgivable at Sunday League level - set up Spain’s Marc Cucurella who could not take full advantage.

View 3 Images Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon were influential in the late first half England turnaround (Image: Matt Lewis - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Ferran Torres went clean through as England’s defence was sliced wide open again. This time, Trafford came out and made a great block. The offside flag went up but Torres was clearly onside and it would have counted. Torres missed another one-on-one.

Tuchel was getting angry on the touchline - and it was easy to see why. In trying to play a bit more like Spain, they were guilty of playing their way into trouble. Spain could have been out of sight.

Then came the most remarkable turnaround. The game turned on its head in the space of four minutes. First, Spain winger Nico Williams lost possession, Elliot Anderson led the break, Anthony Gordon’s flick found Jude Bellingham.

It was Bellingham’s perfectly timed pass which released Gordon and the England winger buried a low shot past Spain keeper Unai Simon. That was more like it for England. Pace, speed and English cut and thrust.

‌



England were ahead after 40 minutes. Gordon’s pass set up O’Reilly and his cross reached Harry Kane and the England captain’s header was deflected in off Cucurella.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel saw his side shoot themselves in the foot against the world champions (Image: Michael Regan/The FA)

From being given the runaround, England were ahead. This felt like they were back at the World Cup, the game slipping away against DR Congo or Norway and then suddenly they showed incredible spirit to haul themselves back into it.

England then wasted a glorious chance to put the game to bed. They were awarded a penalty after VAR ruled Rodri tripped Bellingham.

‌



But inexplicably, Kane smashed the spot kick against the crossbar. Kane’s standing foot slipped in the run-up and that explained his miss. Kane looked crestfallen - and his despair quickly got worse.

Spain drew level on the hour mark. O’Reilly gave the ball away, Dani Olmo set up Spain substitute Alex Baena who steered his low shot from the edge of the box into the bottom corner.

And how Spain made England pay. Baena’s lovely through ball played in Spain substitute Mikel Oyarzabal who dinked the ball past Trafford. The rollercoaster ride was complete.

Bellingham, as ever, was terrific and never stopped trying and even weren’t close in injury time. But it was a case of what might have been.

‌

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel gives reason for surprise Jordan Pickford England decision vs Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel gives reason for surprise Jordan Pickford England decision vs Spain

Thomas Tuchel chose James Trafford as England's goalkeeper ahead of Jordan Pickford to face Spain

View 2 Images Jordan Pickford was named on the bench for England's clash against Spain (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

England manager Thomas Tuchel has explained the reason why he chose to start James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford for the clash against Spain. The Three Lions are facing the reigning world champions at Wembley Stadium on Saturday night in the Nations League.

‌



The clash in London is England’s first match since beating France in the bronze medal match at the World Cup, while it’s Spain’s first game since winning the final against Argentina on July 19 in New Jersey.

‌



Pickford started all of England’s matches on their way to reaching the World Cup semi-final, with Dean Henderson getting the nod for the third-fourth place play-off against France, which ended in a dramatic 6-4 victory for Tuchel’s side.

‌



Trafford starts in goal for England against Spain, with Tuchel explaining that an increase in minutes for the shot-stopper since completing a move to Leeds United in the summer transfer window played a factor in his decision.

The England boss also went on to praise Pickford for the way the Everton goalkeeper reacted to dropping to the bench for the fixture.

"He [Trafford] gets two matches, consecutive matches, because he deserves it, and Pickers [Pickford] gets the other two matches," Tuchel told ITV ahead of kick-off at Wembley.

‌



"It was amazing to see how Jordan Pickford received the message and his reaction to it. We told him that we want to see Trafford at this kind of level in goal.

"We want to use this competition because he has a good start for Leeds, a lot of minutes, he’s starting now, that’s the difference to last season.

"So we want to see what’s behind Pickers, we know what Pickers can give us. He did nothing wrong, and he kept pushing and was very positive about it."

As well as naming Trafford in goal, Tuchel also selected a back four that featured Jarell Quansah, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly.

‌



Elliott Anderson and Myles Lewis-Skelly start in midfield for England against the world champions, just behind Jude Bellingham, who also has Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon on the wings.

Harry Kane also started for England as the Bayern Munich star looks to add to his goal tally for his country.

But the game got off to a less-than-ideal start for Trafford, with Guehi caught in possession on the edge of his own box by Lamine Yamal, who slotted calmly past the England keeper to open the scoring after less than two minutes.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's dig at Pep Guardiola on Man City charges with Man Utd bonus claim
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's dig at Pep Guardiola on Man City charges with Man Utd bonus claim

Jose Mourinho's dig at Pep Guardiola is revisited after a panel found Manchester City breached Premier League rules 114 times, following the original 115 charges

View Image Jose Mourinho has previously given his verdict on Man City's charges (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho has previously taken aim at Pep Guardiola over Manchester City's charges. City, who have consistently denied any wrongdoing, now face an anxious wait to learn their fate after being found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League rules.

‌



The panel determined that City violated the regulations over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, with the club initially charged in 2023. It is understood that the East Manchester outfit, who still maintain their innocence, will challenge the ruling. Questions are now being asked about how, should City's appeal fail, Guardiola's legacy at the Etihad Stadium will be affected.

‌



The Catalan secured a remarkable 17 major trophies at the Etihad Stadium during his 10-year spell. The former Bayern Munich and Barcelona manager has long shared an intense rivalry with ex-Manchester United boss Mourinho.

‌



Man City chairman insists club are INNOCENT in letter after 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

During a 2024 press conference, Guardiola was questioned about the parallels between him celebrating his six titles and Mourinho his three, jokingly expressing hope that his tenure would not conclude in the same fashion as Mourinho's dismissal.

That response and Guardiola highlighting the contrasts in their CVs evidently struck a chord with the Real Madrid boss, who delivered a withering response during a pre-match press conference while Fenerbahce manager.

He said: "Guardiola said something to me yesterday. He won six trophies and I won three, but I won fairly and cleanly. If I lost, I want to congratulate my opponent because he was better than me.

‌



"I don't want to win by dealing with 150 lawsuits."

Speculation is mounting over whether City could be stripped of titles from the period during which they have been found to have violated top-flight regulations.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Such an outcome could see managers such as Mourinho handed winners' medals - and potentially due a payday from their old clubs, opening a can of worms for financial repurcussions across the Premier League.

It was almost two years ago that the now 63-year-old mischievously raised the possibility that his former club, United, could be awarded the 2018 Premier League title held by City.

He said: "I think we still have a chance to win that league... And then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal."

‌



During Mourinho's tenure, United finished as runners-up to City in 2018, his last full season at the helm at Old Trafford.

He was subsequently dismissed in December 2018 following a poor start to the 2018/19 campaign.

Sports.title: Man City braced for major financial blow after 115 charges verdict
Sports.content:
Man City braced for major financial blow after 115 charges verdict

Reports emerged on Friday claiming that Manchester City have been found guilty of alleged financial breaches

View Image Man City were reportedly found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges (Image: Gary Oakley/PA Wire)

Manchester City could reportedly have to deal with the loss of millions of pounds in sponsorship deals if the guilty verdict for the alleged financial breaches stands. News emerged on Friday claiming that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges that had been brought against them by the Premier League.

‌



City were first charged back in 2023, and three years later, a verdict has now emerged, but the club has always maintained their innocence and will now be expected to appeal the outcome of the case.

‌



There will be a wait to discover the full extent of any punishment that City could be forced to deal with if the guilty verdict stands, with ramifications ranging from points deductions to expulsion from the Premier League, as well as past titles being removed.

‌



A report in The Telegraph has now claimed that City face the risk of losing millions in sponsorship deals if the guilty verdict remains.

Man City chairman insists club are INNOCENT in letter after 115 charges verdict READ MORE :

Some of City's sponsors are said to be currently "examining" deals in place with the club, in the event that relegation occurs as a result of the charges.

The report claims that some of City's sponsors may hold the right to renegotiate their deal if the club are relegated from the Premier League, which would likely result in a loss in revenue.

‌



If City are relegated from the Premier League, it would also be likely that the club would not compete in the Champions League next season, which would also see the club miss out on the bonuses that come from competing in Europe’s elite cup competition.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak issued a statement on Saturday in response to the reports that the club had been found guilty of the charges, maintaining his confidence in the club's innocence.

"I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul," he said. "This club matters to me, and you have shown and told me - time and time again - how much Manchester City matters to you. This is why I am writing to you today.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I.

"Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‌



"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

‌



"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium - moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family. Thank you, as always, for your constant support."

City released a statement in response to the update on Friday, which read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

Article continues below

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."
