Their next outing sees them face Czechia in Prague on Tuesday night, live on talkSPORT, kick-off 7:45pm.

Sports.title: England star who pulled out of squad seen down tunnel at Wembley after Spain defeat
Sports.content:
England star who pulled out of squad seen down tunnel at Wembley after Spain defeat

Declan Rice may not have been able to help England on the pitch, but he was still keen to be involved on the night against Spain.

The Arsenal midfielder was one of five players who withdrew from international duty for this break, leaving Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel without one of his trusted lieutenants.



2 Rice was among the tens of thousands who attended England's Nations League clash against Spain Credit: Getty Images - Getty

It was reported that Rice pulled out over load management concerns, especially given he confirmed during the World Cup that he'd been battling nerve pain in his hamstring since December.

But even though he couldn't affect matters on the pitch, Rice made sure he was there for his teammates.

Adrian Durham and Stuart Pearce's verdict on Declan Rice attending Wembley

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham revealed on commentary that Rice was in the tunnel at Wembley, ready to greet the England players as they walked off the field following the 3-2 loss to Spain.



"That's a good thing, isn't it," Durham said.

"You know he's a leader in that side."

Former England captain Stuart Pearce agreed with Durham's sentiment and stated Rice's presence would give his international teammates a 'lift'.

"It's absolutely no surprise to me at all," Pearce said.

"When they were talking about players dropping out the squad, Declan Rice isn't one of those individuals that I ever question or would ever question. You know his heart's with this team.



"He's proved that with performance after performance and it always gives you a lift, him being here tonight."

How England's loss to Spain unfolded

Rice would have been an anxious spectator on Saturday as he watched England fall agonisingly short of beating the world champions.



2 England have not beaten Spain since October 2018 Credit: Getty

Tuchel's side proved to be the architects of their own downfall, and that was on show within the opening two minutes due to a Marc Guehi howler.

The Manchester City defender turned back towards goal, only for Lamine Yamal to be lurking right behind.

Yamal happily robbed Guehi of the ball before clipping past James Trafford to put Spain ahead.



However, England roared back to life and took a 2-1 lead courtesy of goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane.

Kane then had a golden opportunity to double the host's advantage when England were awarded a penalty in the second half, only to clatter his effort against the crossbar.

Spain then pulled level through Alex Baena on the hour mark after Nico O'Reilly lost the ball in a dangerous area before Mikel Oyarzabal netted the winner in the 74th minute.

England return to action on Tuesday when they take on Czechia in Prague, with kick-off scheduled for 7:45pm, live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Roy Keane calls out Cole Palmer for his ‘bad habits’ after England withdrawal
Sports.content:
Roy Keane calls out Cole Palmer for his ‘bad habits’ after England withdrawal

Roy Keane has downplayed the prospect of Cole Palmer bringing England to another level as he called out the player's 'bad habits'.

The Manchester United legend was dismissive of the Chelsea talisman's influence ahead of the Three Lions' 3-2 defeat to Spain.

3 Palmer's England commitment has been called into question Credit: Getty

Palmer was recalled by Thomas Tuchel for his Nations League squad after missing out on the World Cup last summer.

However, the 24-year-old withdrew from the fixtures alongside Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento.

Palmer's absence drew the most headlines, having played the full 90 minutes in Chelsea's 3-0 defeat at Brentford last week.

It is the second occasion that the 14-cap international has been called up for England and pulled out since Tuchel took charge in 2025.

Why is Palmer being criticised?

Palmer, who has also missed three England camps entirely with injury, was described as managing his load with his latest withdrawal.

He said during a Twitch live stream last week that ‘I had one leg for ten months’, but has featured in all seven of Chelsea's competitive games this term, with six starts and five full 90 minute run-outs.

In contrast, fellow withdrawers Mainoo and Rashford both earned the trust of Tuchel, having been part of his squad in the US.

Livramento, who was forced to miss England's World Cup campaign through injury, also sat out Newcastle’s win over Hull last weekend.

And Rice, who played through the pain barrier at the tournament, underlined his international commitment by showing up at Wembley as a spectator to support the squad against Spain.

3 Tuchel has had Palmer for just three England fixtures Credit: Getty

Cole Palmer England availability under Tuchel March 2025: Palmer called up but then injured before camp

May 2025: Palmer called up and played away to Andorra

August 2025: Palmer not called up due to groin issue

October 2025: Palmer not called up due to injury

November 2025: Palmer not called up amid continuing fitness issue

March 2026: Palmer called up and played against both Uruguay and Japan

May 2026: Palmer left out of World Cup squad

September 2026: Palmer called up, withdrew due to injury

Roy Keane hits out at Palmer

Asked about Palmer's absence ahead of England's defeat to Spain, Keane played down the influence that the Chelsea star would have.

"Well, I think, whatever his injuries, and if he is injured… I watched his last game against Brentford and if you think he’s going to get England to another level and win trophies, forget about it," Keane told ITV.

"I like Palmer, he’s a talented boy, but he’s got far too many bad habits, for me."

Keane's criticism comes just days after England head coach Tuchel warned Palmer that he misses 'too many opportunities'.

Tuchel said: "I can only judge him on what he [Palmer] is delivering for the national team, and he's just missing too many opportunities.

3 Palmer has six goal involvements in seven games for Chelsea Credit: Getty

"If Declan [Rice] calls me, and he explains to me, and I see against Brighton straight away that something is off that confirmed that impression; every case is different.

"I know from Marcus [Rashford] and Kobbie [Mainoo] that they play with discomfort for their clubs. I know it looks strange if Kobbie and Marcus finish a game at the weekend for their clubs and then suddenly are not here, but okay - first of all, in doubt, we trust the players.

"I have no reason not to trust the players because they were with us in the US and they were fantastic. Tino Livramento also pulled out. This is normal.

"I just refuse to put too much into it. I refuse to believe it."

Sports.title: Former Champions League club saved from liquidation after being bought for 86p
Sports.content:
Former Champions League club saved from liquidation after being bought for 86p

French side Bordeaux have staved off liquidation thanks to an English investment firm.

The club, which competed in the Champions League as recently as 2010, find themselves down in the sixth tier of French football amid a litany of financial issues.

2 There may finally be brighter days ahead for Bordeaux Credit: AFP

But Bordeaux have since been rescued by Park Bench, who will take control of the club from Gerard Lopez for just €1 (86p).

Who is behind the English investment firm purchasing Bordeaux?

At the helm of Park Bench is James Bord, a poker professional who unsuccessfully tried to purchase Sheffield Wednesday.

Bord was named as the preferred bidder for the Owls last December but the prospective takeover ultimately collapsed.

He has since switched focus to Bordeaux, with the deal to acquire the club announced at the Tribunal de Commerce, per French publication Sud-Ouest.

How is the deal to purchase Bordeaux structured?

The outlet adds that the sale of the club would result in a renegotiation of its debts, which would need to be paid over 12 years.

Bordeaux's debt, at present, sits at €26m (£22m).

However, as part of the deal, the debt would lower to €13m (£11m).

Fans of Bordeaux, who competed in Ligue 1 as recently as five years ago, will hope that Bord's mooted acquisition sparks life back into the club.

Bordeaux's difficult recent history

The six-time Ligue 1 champions have endured a tumultuous few years and were forced to renounce their professional status in July 2024.

Bordeaux had been a professional team since 1937.

2 Andy Carroll spent the 2024/25 campaign with Bordeaux, scoring 11 goals Credit: AFP

Prior to Bordeaux giving up their professional status, it was hoped Liverpool's owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), would come to the rescue.

However, negotiations ultimately broke down.

Bordeaux spent last season competing in Championnat National 2, the fourth tier of French football.

The club finished second in the competition with 62 points, three behind winners La Roche.

Yet it mattered little as the club's financial issues meant they were still relegated.

Sports.title: Three England players and Tuchel get brutal 2/10 ratings as manager slammed for decision that ‘made no sense’
Sports.content:
Three England players and Tuchel get brutal 2/10 ratings as manager slammed for decision that ‘made no sense’

England missed a golden opportunity to beat world champions Spain with a catalogue of errors leading to a 3-2 defeat at Wembley.

The Three Lions found themselves 2-1 up at the break, but a Harry Kane missed penalty proved the catalyst for another collapse.

6 England threw away another lead in a big game Credit: Getty

England had initially done well to recover from a Marc Guehi howler that allowed Lamine Yamal to open the scoring inside two minutes.

Thomas Tuchel's side battled back to lead at the break through Anthony Gordon and Kane, and then had a golden chance for three.

However, Kane missed from the penalty spot, and a rejuvenated Spain made the most of the let-off by turning the game on its head.

"It was a great game of football," Durham said post-match. "Can't help feeling absolutely gutted as all the players shake hands."

The voice of talkSPORT continued: "I think some of the Tuchel substitutions I don't know burst a bubble inside this stadium.

"I thought a lot of fans were wondering, 'Why on earth is he making those substitutions? We've been there before, haven't we?'

Read below for the full player ratings from talkSPORT's Adrian Durham...

Quick off the Marc

An unforgivable schoolboy error from defender Guehi, who left England with a mountain to climb after just a minute at Wembley.

It was Guehi's huge howler in a 3-3 draw with Everton that effectively ended Manchester City's Premier League title challenge in May.

6 England trailed after two minutes due to Guehi's major mistake Credit: Getty

Months later, the 26-year-old had another major gaffe, but for his country, as he dawdled in possession with his first touch on the ball.

Ignoring the opportunity to pass to Nico O'Reilly, he instead turned blind towards his goalkeeper and had his pocket picked by Lamine Yamal, who raced clear to slot past James Trafford.

Considering his Man City teammate O'Reilly was then hugely culpable for Spain's equaliser, Durham questioned whether the fact that the club have been found guilty of the majority of their FFP charges had any part in distracting the two defenders.

England legend Stuart Pearce replied: "I wouldn't think so. I'll be very, very surprised if that is the case.

"The bottom line is City are so used to dominating the ball, sometimes they've got to check out - recycle it and whatever.

"Tonight there was some good pressing from the Spaniards, and it caught us out."

6 Durham claimed O'Reilly was all over the place at times and awarded him a 2/10 Credit: Getty

Flash Gordon

The scorer of England's goal in the World Cup semi-final, now playing in Spain, popped up with another big strike - fittingly against La Roja.

Gordon spoke at length about the Three Lions' identity in the pre-match press conference, and the fact that his equaliser came from pace and power on the counter-attack rather than tiki-taka football underlined his argument.

His now-El Clasico rival Jude Bellingham was the man who drove forward and slipped him in, and the Barcelona winger did the rest by slotting past Unai Simon into the near post.

The winger was taken off on 70 minutes, with Durham slamming Tuchel for that decision, which he believes 'made no sense.'

6 Gordon is the first-ever England player to score more than once against the number- one FIFA-ranked team (since their inception in 1992) Credit: Getty

Ballon War

Kane answered the goalscoring call from his Ballon d'Or rival with his fortuitous header deflecting off Cucurella to give England the lead.

However, the Bayern Munich talisman fluffed his big moment to pull clear of Yamal from the penalty spot when he rattled the crossbar.

Kane, who has memories of missing from 12 yards for his country against a European powerhouse, gave himself a sense of deja vu.

He had scored nine penalties since missing that effort against France in 2022, but his spot-kick run ended in emphatic fashion at Wembley.

Awarded a 7/10 by Durham, who asked whether Kane's slip was unlucky or a lack of care and attention in the preparation.

6 Kane has missed a penalty for England for the first time since the 2022 World Cup against France Credit: Getty

Pearce replied: "No, I think it's just unfortunate where he's planted his foot. Sometimes you plant your foot with a solid set of full studs, and he's just had a slight slip underneath it.

"Saying that it didn't affect the contact he had on the ball. It's a really solid contact, and he's ended up hitting the underside of the ball.

"It's almost a perfect penalty, if you like, but the double touch that the referees managed to notice.

"He'll be disappointed in that, as I say he's missed six penalties now; that's quite a few."

6

Sports.title: Man City in danger of football oblivion as Premier League eye ground-breaking sanction
Sports.content:
The EFL are willing to work in tandem with the Premier League to punish Manchester City, talkSPORT understands.

Although City have been found guilty of a significant amount of financial breaches, they are yet to be reprimanded.



2 Enzo Maresca has walked into a firestorm at City Credit: Getty

And whatever punishment City receive, it is anticipated the club will appeal it.

In essence, that mean a conclusion to the ordeal could be months, potentially years away.

However, several parties, including Simon Jordan, have cautioned City over the merits of launching an appeal and expecting the initial verdict to be overturned.



Unfortunately for City, the majority of punishments that have been floated are severe as the Premier League seeks justice.

But Jacobs warned it's not just the Premier League that City may need to worry about.



Ben Jacobs explains how the EFL could get involved in Manchester City's case

"My understanding is the Premier League have been pushing for a significant, a record, a ground-breaking, a severe points deduction, and even having Manchester City relegated," Jacobs said.

"I can also exclusively tell you that if Manchester City are kicked out of the Premier League, the EFL plan to read the verdict, and they are willing, in solidarity, to back the Premier League position and try to keep Manchester City out of the EFL as well.



"So there's a danger in a doomsday scenario that Manchester City could be kicked out of football altogether.

However, Jacobs was at pains to stress that expulsion is only one legal possibility.

As for the points deduction, Jacobs outlined there are a number of ways in which it could be handed down.

2 City could find themselves not just booted from the Premier League, but also the EFL Credit: Getty



How Manchester City could be impacted by points deductions

One possibility is that City receive a points deduction in the range of 50-55 points, which Jacobs described as a 'de facto relegation'.

Any more points and Jacobs believed it would be an 'automatic relegation'.

However, should City be docked anywhere between 30 to 40 points but accrue 80 points during the season, it could very well be enough to keep them up.

Jacobs added that in the conversations he's had regarding the matter, there's also the chance City receive a points deduction that is spread across multiple seasons.



That would prove especially damaging to City's Champions League aspirations, robbing them of the riches and prestige that comes with competing in the tournament.

However, Jacobs cautioned that City copping a penalty of that ilk could be seen as 'quite a prejudiced punishment'.

Regardless, it appears a final, definitive verdict on City's financial indiscretions may be some time away.

Sports.title: Ashley Young’s son Tyler joins eighth-tier club after leaving Premier League Ipswich
Sports.content:
The football career of Ashley Young's son will continue.

Lincolnshire-based Stamford, who play in the Southern League Premier Central division, announced they have signed Tyler Young.

2 Tyler Young has found a new home Credit: Getty

Young is one of five new arrivals at Stamford, including Mark Jones, Ronnie Walker, Zhani Burgess and Dan Lawlor.

Stamford also announced the departures of Cheyenne Loureiro, Giovanni Loureiro and Trey Charles.

Tyler Young's career at a glance

Young joined following a brief spell at National League South side Walton and Hersham.

The 20-year-old, who plays as a midfielder, made just two appearances for the club before he moved to Stamford.

Young was a free agent earlier this summer following his release from Ipswich Town.

He developed in the academies of Arsenal and QPR before he penned senior terms with League One outfit Peterborough United in 2024.

Young went on to make just one senior appearance for the Posh.

When Ashley Young almost played his son in FA Cup

There was a chance the midfielder could have taken the field opposite his legendary father when Everton met Peterborough in the third round of the FA Cup in January 2025.

Although the elder Young got on the pitch, then-Posh boss Darren Ferguson opted not to bring on the Everton star's son.

Ferguson later explained he was hoping to send Young on but with his side trailing by just one goal, he opted to roll the dice on a striker.

2 The pair could've made history as the first father-son match-up in FA Cup history had they been on the pitch at the same time Credit: PA

The decision not to let Young share the pitch with his son sparked outrage from several quarters, including from the Red Devils legend himself.

Luckily for Young, he soon got the opportunity to become teammates with his son when the latter joined Ipswich last September.

However, the pair never got to share the pitch as Young's son got shipped out on loan to non-league outfits Chatham Town and Potters Bar Town.

Young Sr opted to retire at the end of the 2025/26 campaign having helped Ipswich secure promotion back to the Premier League while his son got released.

How have Stamford performed this season?

The 20-year-old has now wound up at Stamford, who have endured a difficult start to the 2026/27 Southern League Premier Central Division campaign.

Stamford sit last in the competition having lost all four of their league fixtures.

Worryingly, they have scored just one goal and conceded 21, both of which are league-leading figures.

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham wonderkid wants to stay grounded despite stunning form after exit
Sports.content:
Ex-Tottenham wonderkid wants to stay grounded despite stunning form after exit

Ex-Tottenham striker Will Lankshear has promised not to take his foot off the gas but has a long way to go before a senior England call-up.

The Middlesbrough star continued his fine start to the season by scoring on his Three Lions Under-21 debut against Kazakhstan.

3 Lankshear - on his Under-21s debut - scored England's fourth of the game Credit: Getty

Lankshear netted England's fourth in a 4-2 comeback victory for Lee Carsley's side at Molineux on Friday evening.

The Young Lions are now six points ahead of Slovakia in Group D with two games remaining, and are on the brink of qualifying for Euro 2027 as they seek a third successive title.

Lankshear poked home Jobe Bellingham's cross to seal the win after Ali Turganov's own goal and strikes from Josh Acheampong and Max Alleyne.

The 21-year-old now boasts a tally of nine goals in 12 matches this season, with six in eight for Championship promotion-chasing Boro.

Will Lankshear reacts to England U21 debut

On his goalscoring debut for England's U21s, he told talkSPORT's Ian Abrahams post-match: "An extremely proud moment for me.

"When I got the call from Lee to come along to this camp, I was over the moon.

"When I got the chance to come on tonight, I really wanted to make an impact and try and score a goal, and I did."

"Of course," Lankshear replied when asked if he had it in his head that whatever he did against Kazakhstan, he wanted to end up with a goal.

"I think for me, coming into this, I was left out of the last two squads, to be fair. So, coming into this one, I really wanted to try and make an impression. I feel like I've had a good training week.

"I love coming here, and I love representing the badge. I've done it for the 19s and 20s, now 21s. It's a really, really proud moment for me.

3 Lankshear will win a senior England cap before long, according to Adrian Durham Credit: Getty

"Every single time I step onto the pitch, I just want to do my best."

Lankshear on his current form

The forward joined Boro on a five-year deal last summer for an initial £10million plus a potential £10million in add-ons.

Having previously scored 11 league goals for relegated Oxford United on loan last year, Lankshear is firing on all fronts right now.

"It really is going really well," he said. "But obviously for me, I just want to stay grounded. I really want to work hard. I've still got a lot to do.

"I've still got a long way to go this season. This is just the start. It's really exciting, and I won't take the foot off the gas."

Lankshear on senior England call-up

Adrian Durham recently backed uncapped Lankshear to lead the line for England at Euro 2028 as his stock continues to rise.

3 Spurs have been warned by Durham they have made the 'biggest transfer mistake ever' by selling Lankshear Credit: Getty

However, the man himself is keeping his feet firmly on the ground when asked if he has the next major tournament in his sights.

"I'd just focus on the present. Every day, getting better. I'm still miles away from that at the moment," Lankshear said.

"I've still got a long, long way to go, and I'll continue to improve. Hopefully that's the aim at some point in my career.

"That's the aim of all of us players in there. To represent the country and bring something home for the country.

"But I've still got a long, long way to go, and we'll see!"

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel concedes England's Man City stars could have been distracted by guilty verdict after Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly gaffes in Spain defeat
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel rued the England errors which stopped his side from ending Spain's remarkable 39-game unbeaten run, admitting his players were 'punished' at Wembley.

The first two goals conceded by the Three Lions came directly after Manchester City duo Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly each gave away the ball respectively. Tuchel also described the defending for Spain's winner from substitute Mikel Oyarzabal as not good enough.

England's manager did concede his players – and particularly those from City – could have been distracted by the bombshell news surrounding their club.

When asked if it had been a distraction, Tuchel said: 'Not for me but I can imagine maybe for the Manchester City players. For me, not. I will not comment on that because it is an ongoing court case. I didn't make it a topic. It was not a topic for me.

'The players have more time than me, they have one training session, so for sure, I can imagine that they talk about it. But it's good that they do. I don't feel it distracted.'

England came from behind to lead Spain at half-time and Harry Kane had the chance to make it 3-1 after Jude Bellingham won a penalty, but Tuchel's striker crashed his spot-kick into the crossbar. That sparked the beginning of the Spanish comeback.

Marc Guehi gifted Spain the early opening goal when he was dispossessed by Lamine Yamal

Guehi's Manchester City team-mate Nico O'Reilly gave the ball away for Spain's equaliser

'We wanted to be the team desperate to beat them,' Tuchel said. 'The reality is we lost.'

On the defensive mistakes, Tuchel added: 'It is what it is. It happens. It happened too often and we got punished at the highest level. We made the worst possible start against a team like Spain who love to control the game and play with confidence and on the ball.

'It happened. The reaction was OK. It cost us a little confidence, that is normal. We had another two big mistakes in build-up situations and conceded two big chances and survived those chances.

'We scored the equaliser. We scored the second goal. We could have scored a third goal in the first half. We should absolutely have scored a third one in the second half.

'That would have been the decisive punch to get this full momentum and belief. We couldn't do it. Then unfortunately another technical mistake cost us. Then the momentum shifted again. We conceded one goal from open play which we should absolutely defend better.

'The result is not what we wanted. I think we could have won it. We have to live with it, recover from it, learn from it. Do what we did on the same level and reduce and improve our mistakes.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Furious Premier League clubs set to trigger £800MILLION lawsuits against Man City after seismic 115 charges verdict - as lawyers prepare for case to drag on for another TWO YEARS
Sports.content:
Revealed: Furious Premier League clubs set to trigger £800MILLION lawsuits against Man City after seismic 115 charges verdict - as lawyers prepare for case to drag on for another TWO YEARS

The Premier League's seismic victory over Manchester City will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800m – although the case itself may rumble on for another TWO YEARS, Daily Mail Sport understands.

On Friday, this newspaper reported how City had been found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the competition’s 115 charges against them for financial doping. It can now be disclosed that the Premier League has succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims.

On Saturday, the club hit back in the shape of a strong statement from chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, who declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’, - with an appeal seen as inevitable. In a letter to fans, he added: ‘we have faced challenges before and prevailed’.

Despite City’s stance, and while an official verdict remains unannounced, a quartet of rivals are understood to be already preparing their own legal cases.

In late 2024, Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight - be found guilty.

Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City’s cheating.

A quartet of rivals are understood to be already preparing their own legal cases against Man City after they were found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the 115 charges against them

Liverpool and Man United are among four clubs in 2024 to have reserved their right to take action in the event that City be found guilty. Pictured: Owners John W Henry and Sir Jim Ratcliffe

Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak released a strong statement, declared that they remain confident of clearing their name and ‘proving the club’s innocence’

It is thought that those who feel most badly done to, with Tottenham having missed out on a Champions League spot on a number of occasions, will ask for the biggest sums.

According to those with knowledge of the situation, £200m would not be an outrageous estimate.

However, City are expected to appeal a verdict that has sent shockwaves through football.

Aided by an expensively-assembled team of lawyers, they managed to overturn a two-year Champions League ban handed down by UEFA in 2020, after they were initially found to have committed ‘serious breaches’ of the governing body’s financial fair play regulations between 2012 to 2016.

That case was heard at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland. While that route is not available to them given this is a Premier League case, there is an appeal process and both parties would need to be satisfied with the make-up of another three-person panel who would rule on whether the verdict is sound.

Against UEFA, City’s team was led by Paul Harris KC, along with Lord David Pannick KC. Legal experts have already noted that Pannick is viewed primarily as an appellate lawyer, who specialises in such matters. Given what is at stake, it is unlikely that City’s Abu Dhabi ownership will leave any stone unturned as they seek to overturn the judgement. Some within the legal industry believe that if the appeal fails they could head to the High Court, and have estimated that there may not be a conclusion for another two years.

In a lengthy statement, Al Mubarak seemed to make the suggestion that the process had not been fair. He asked fans to study a statement made on Friday by the club closely. That statement read: ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

In his message to fans, he wrote: ‘The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began..

‘There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

‘While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club. We will not give them that opportunity.’

Sports.title: Roy Keane tells 'cheating' Man City to 'take their medicine' after guilty verdict - and REJECTS Rodri's claims titles were deserved despite 'vast majority' of 115 charges being proven
Sports.content:
Roy Keane tells 'cheating' Man City to 'take their medicine' after guilty verdict - and REJECTS Rodri's claims titles were deserved despite 'vast majority' of 115 charges being proven

Roy Keane has warned 'cheating' Manchester City deserve a harsh punishment after being found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 Premier League charges against them.

The Premier League accused the club of widespread financial doping over an era of sustained success and Daily Mail Sport understands they have succeeded in proving all of the substantive claims.

City have won 26 trophies since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, including eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups and the Champions League as part of their 2023 Treble-winning season.

Expulsion and stripping City of their titles are among the sanctions available following the ruling, which the club are set to appeal.

And ex-Manchester United captain Keane told City they will have to 'take their medicine' because they deserve to be punished. He also rejected claims from Rodri that the titles and trophies the club won during that time had been 'deserved' - despite most of the charges now being proven.

'It's about time,' Keane said on ITV. 'It has obviously been going on a long time now. I would disagree with Rodri's messages there. It was the club's choice - they chose to cheat.

'Whatever they have won over the last few years, they deserve to be punished. Where we start and finish with that is difficult but they were cheating. They've been found guilty of it and they have to take their medicine now. It was a shock to be found guilty of so many of the charges.'

Roy Keane has called for Manchester City to be given a harsh punishment after the guilty verdict

The Premier League have accused City of widespread financial doping over an era of sustained success

Ian Wright also called for the club to be hit with severe sanctions. 'They should be punished for it,' he said.

'They may have been able to experience those memories and all those great times together but when you look at the teams chasing them who were doing it right, it's not right.

'What have we taken from Liverpool and Klopp's legacy, and that team? What could they have experienced? They cheated to get it done and other players have missed out on that.'

City deny wrongdoing and are set to appeal the decision. On Saturday, chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said the club is confident it will clear its name.

In a letter to fans, Al Mubarak writes that, despite reporting, the Premier League's process 'still has a long way to run' and adds 'our confidence in proving the club's innocence remains as strong as it was when this began'.

'We have faced challenges before and prevailed,' he added.

Daily Mail Sport also reported the Premier League's victory over Manchester City will trigger a series of legal claims for as much as £800m – although the case itself may rumble on for another two years.

Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United served formal notices reserving their right to take action in the event that City – who could now face expulsion from the top flight - be found guilty.

Representatives have already begun putting together a case on how much they feel they have a claim for, pointing out that they have lost potential income on the back of City's cheating.

It is thought that those who feel most badly done to, with Tottenham having missed out on a Champions League spot on a number of occasions, will ask for the biggest sums.

According to those with knowledge of the situation, £200m would not be an outrageous estimate.

Sports.title: Ireland goalkeeper REFUSES to play against Israel in protest at Gaza 'atrocities': Controversial clash to go ahead after FOUR-HOUR talks and last-minute vote among players
Sports.content:
Ireland goalkeeper REFUSES to play against Israel in protest at Gaza 'atrocities': Controversial clash to go ahead after FOUR-HOUR talks and last-minute vote among players

Irish keeper Gavin Bazunu defended his decision to pull out of Ireland's controversial Nations League clash against Israel by insisting he isn't against Israelis or Jews – but against the atrocities in Gaza.

The second-choice stopper made the comments at the end of a day of high drama which saw the men's national side take a vote over whether to proceed with the match following Bazunu letting his feelings be known at the team hotel in Debrecen, Hungary on Saturday.

According to former Irish manager Brian Kerr, that vote occurred in the absence of Bazunu and ended 14-8 in favour of fulfilling the fixture. The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has refused to confirm or deny those figures.

And in further criticism Kerr called on the FAI board to resign and accused them of 'collaborating' in Israeli sportswashing.

After a tense day where the match was plunged into doubt, Bazunu wrote on Instagram: 'Representing my country means everything to me.

'I have the utmost respect for every single one of my teammates, the manager, his staff and the Irish people.

View this post on Instagram

Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has withdrawn from the squad for the clash with Israel

'However, I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly. I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle, therefore I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel.

'My decision is based purely upon my belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong. It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.

'There are few times when you get a chance in life to stand for something bigger and I strongly believe that this is one of them.'

A source close to the player last night told The Mail on Sunday the Dubliner's family is proud of him for standing up for his beliefs.

'Gavin is a hero,' they said. ´What he's done took great courage. His family is proud.'

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had earlier confirmed that Bazunu will not play in Sunday's fixture.

Hallgrimsson had previously stirred controversy after saying his team are 'playing against genocide' amid Israel's attacks on Palestine, where more than 70,000 people have been killed since the war in Gaza began.

Hallgrimsson's comments sparked an angry backlash from Israeli officials, but there have been growing calls for the game to be scrapped by the Irish public – with a petition attracting over 17,000 signatures.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel should be feeling the pressure after this calamitous defensive display: The German needs to convince England fans they are moving forward but familiar problem remains, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
An exciting night at Wembley but not the result that England wanted against the world champions.

Exciting going forward but a calamity at the back, Thomas Tuchel's side have started an important Nations League campaign with a defeat.

Here Daily Mail Sport look at the good, the bad and the ugly of another setback for England against a top ten team.

Tuchel under pressure

The FA remain convinced that Thomas Tuchel is the man to take English football forward but in the eyes of the public, the 53-year-old will now start to feel a little pressure.

Certainly Tuesday's game in Czechia suddenly feels very big indeed. Tuchel's team were a real threat with the ball here. They made a usually parsimonious Spain defence look very ordinary.

The FA remain convinced that Thomas Tuchel is the man to take English football forward

Had Harry Kane not slipped in missing a penalty early in the second half, England would probably have won

Had Harry Kane not slipped in missing a penalty early in the second half, England would probably have won. But the fact is that they didn't. They lost.

And this adds fuel to the argument that England tend to struggle against good teams. Tuchel will present World Cup wins against Croatia and France (in a meaningless third-placed game) as evidence to the contrary.

And there was that memorable night in Mexico, of course. But Tuchel needs to convince people that his team are moving forward as we approach a home Euros in 2028 and a night like this – when his team gives the opposition endless chances with poor use of the ball – doesn't help him.

Afterwards winger Anthony Gordon tried to accentuate the positives when he said: 'We can win that game so easily. I think you've seen here tonight that we're a top team.'

Top teams don't ship three goals at home, whoever they play. This was not a brave or plucky defeat. It just a defeat.

Limited options across the back

This was a calamitous defensive performance by England and former centre half Matthew Upson put it well when he said: 'I want to see more of the boring stuff, not the high octane stuff.'

Tuchel's back four maybe had taken too much notice of all the pre-match chat about English DNA and seemed intent on playing their way up the field even when more direct options would have served them better.

How many chances did Spain have as a result of an Englishman giving the ball away? Half a dozen maybe? It was painful to watch and seemed to be catching.

This was not a night that Marc Guehi will want to remember after his hand in Spain's opener

Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite had only been on the field a matter of moments when he passed the ball straight to a red shirt.

He got away with that one but on the whole England did not and it will be interesting to see what Tuchel does on Tuesday night in Prague.

He can swap his left backs – Lewis Hall for Nico O'Reilly – but doesn't trust Trent Alexander Arnold defensively over on the other side.

As for his central defenders, this was not a night Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa will want to remember but will Tuchel really want to hand responsibility to Branthwaite and Trevoh Chalobah on Tuesday? It's hard to see it.

Gordon could be the future

This was a night when England impressed going forward. 'We're playing against the world champions,' said Kane. 'And we went toe-to-toe'.

This was a sign of what this team could become if only they get other parts of their game right and Anthony Gordon typified that. The Gordon we saw here was the one we needed at the World Cup.

The Liverpudlian was aggressive and purposeful and dangerous. Why he was taken off with 20 minutes to go was a mystery. A move to a really big club can either daunt a player or infuse with them confidence.

For Gordon, it seems as though his summer move from Newcastle to Barcelona has filled him with the belief that he belongs on the biggest stage. Here, he frightened the Spain defence throughout with straight line running, good delivery and an ability and will to drift in from his wing on occasion and cause damage through the middle.

Anthony Gordon has the chance to lock down a place on the left for the foreseeable future

His goal was a case in point. The one-two he played with Jude Bellingham was lovely and he took advantage of poor positioning from Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon to score with a firm low shot.

Much of the absentee talk ahead of this game was about Cole Palmer but Marcus Rashford's withdrawal has allowed Gordon to lock down the spot on the left for the foreseeable future and this was a good start.

The race is on

Tuchel's decision to replace Jordan Pickford was a bold one. Pickford has 91 caps and has grown into a truly top-class goalkeeper. But I get the sense that the England manager has been waiting for James Trafford to play regularly at club level – as he is now at Leeds – before giving him some games.

Trafford is the one he sees England's long-term No 1 but it's interesting that Tuchel plans to play both goalkeepers during this four-game spell of games. 'He gets two consecutive matches because he deserves and then Pickford gets the other two,' explained Tuchel before kick-off. 'The decision is half and half.'

Back in the 1980s, English football had a spell when Peter Shilton and Ray Clemence shared goalkeeping duties on a rotation basis but it doesn't feel like a solution for Tuchel going forward.

He is going to have to decide and the race is now on. Trafford did nothing much wrong here playing behind a back four that simply must have terrified him.

A mixed night for Rodri

The fact former Manchester City midfielder Rodri is one of the few defensive players ever to win the Ballon D'Or says everything for the depth of his ability. Late in the first half at Wembley, he received the ball under pressure in this own penalty area, turned away from two English players and ran past two more to find space in midfield.

Within ten seconds, Spain were creating a chance at the other end of the field. The 30-year-old didn't have it all his own way, though. He was left standing by O'Reilly's run as England created a goal for Kane and then poked a foot out for Bellingham to tumble over for a penalty that Kane subsequently missed.

Some of that was down to the pressure being exerted by England's attacking play. Despite their issues at the back, England were a real threat going forward. They made a normally resolute Spanish defence look very ordinary at time.

They have to try and use that as a positive heading to Prague on Tuesday night.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel is developing an unfortunate habit - his unique selling point was supposed to be dragging England across the line but he was again powerless as Spain expose gulf in class, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
In England’s first proper game since Thomas Tuchel blew the chance of beating Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals and blamed it on England’s history and traditions, we learned a little more about the manager’s DNA in the Nations League defeat to world champions Spain at Wembley. Tuchel was powerless to help England keep their lead against Lionel Messi and co in Atlanta in July and he was powerless to help them protect their advantage against Spain at a sold-out Wembley last night. It is getting to be rather an unfortunate habit for a boss whose unique selling point was supposed to be dragging England across the line. England had the chance to go into a 3-1 lead early in the second half when Harry Kane, who had already scored the 86th goal of his remarkable England career in the first half, stood over a penalty. But Kane slipped as he took it and double-hit it against the crossbar. England crumbled after that. The hard truth is that even though England led at half-time, the opening 45 minutes had exposed a gulf between them and Luis de la Fuente’s side, reigning world and European Champions, whose unbeaten run now stretches to 39 games. They thoroughly deserved their 3-2 victory. Spain sliced England apart time after time in that first half and it was only their profligacy which allowed Tuchel’s side to maintain a foothold in the match. If this had been billed as the World Cup final that never was, there was a crumb of comfort in Spain’s superiority. There were bright points for England. Anthony Gordon was a constant threat down the England left, Jude Bellingham was as authoritative and as classy as ever and Elliot Anderson was a fine anchor at the base of midfield. But there was no sign that England are getting closer to dethroning Spain as the world’s best team. They are poles apart in quality. England crumbled after Harry Kane missed from the penalty spot in a 3-2 defeat by Spain Thomas Tuchel was powerless to help the Three Lions protect their advantage against Spain To complete a chastening 36 hours for Manchester City, two of their players, Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly, gifted Spain their first two goals with careless defending. After the news the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges laid against them, two mistakes was the last thing they needed. Kane will have taken some comfort from getting on the scoresheet but his missed penalty will not have advanced his cause in his battle with Spain’s Lamine Yamal and France’s Kylian Mbappe for the Ballon d’Or. Yamal suggested the prize should go to him or Mbappe and the goal he scored inside two minutes was a sign of his class. England move to their next match in Czechia on Tuesday in an uncertain state. They are becalmed and Tuchel’s attempt to blame their World Cup exit on his players has backfired. Five players pulled out of the squad last week. There are suggestions of some disquiet in the camp. Tuchel chose to start with Jarell Quansah at right-back rather than Trent Alexander-Arnold. Quansah is a fine player but to start him at right-back ahead of one of the best technically gifted players in the world, at a time when England’s ability to keep the ball is under the spotlight, was dispiriting. The pre-game minute’s applause for Kevin Keegan, the former England manager who died in July, had scarcely faded when Spain took the lead. It came courtesy of an uncharacteristic mistake from Guehi. Guehi got the ball on the edge of the England area, looked over his shoulder and saw Yamal closing him down. Guehi tried to turn away from danger but turned straight into it instead. Yamal stole the ball away from him, held him off with ease and clipped the ball past James Trafford. Trafford, who had been picked ahead of Jordan Pickford, must have wondered what he had got himself into. Ferran Torres, the scorer of the goal that won the World Cup final, had the ball in the back of the net a couple of minutes later but had strayed offside. England kept giving the ball away as they overplayed it. They were trying to beat Spain at their own game. They should have heeded the warning of Anthony Gordon, who has made such a fine start to life at Barcelona. Kane slipped before hitting his penalty against the crossbar in a rare miss from the England captain Mikel Oyarzabal's delicious chip was worthy of winning any game as the world champions claimed a deserved victory Kane's header went in off Marc Cucurella to give England the lead before half-time ‘We can’t keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we’re not them,’ Gordon said last week. Ten minutes later, Yamal threaded a delicious through-ball into the path of Torres, who was played onside by Quansah as he burst forward. Torres ran clean in on Trafford but this time, the England goalkeeper was equal to it and blocked his shot. England were being sliced apart. Spain missed another golden opportunity to extend their lead 20 minutes before half-time. Anderson gave the ball away to Rodri and Rodri punished him with a slide-rule pass that put Torres clean through. Torres drilled the ball wide. The chances kept coming. Yamal freed Olmo with an extravagant backheel and Olmo lashed a shot across Trafford but just wide. Spain might have been four goals ahead. They were teaching England a football lesson. Then, as is often the way, England equalised. It was a brilliant counter-attacking goal. Anderson started it on the edge of the England area and played the ball forward to Gordon. Gordon flicked it into the path of Jude Bellingham and Bellingham chose the perfect moment to play the ball back to him. Real Madrid and Barcelona in harmony. Gordon ran on to it and slotted the ball home. Parity was more than England deserved but five minutes later, they were ahead. Kane had just bent a shot narrowly wide when he got ahead of his marker and nodded a cross from Nico O’Reilly goalwards. Marc Cucurella tried to intercept it but it bounced off the top of his thigh and past Simon Eight minutes after the break, England should have gone further ahead. Bellingham was brought down in the box by Rodri and Kane took the penalty. But his left foot slipped when he planted it and he smashed the spot kick against the crossbar. After an hour, Spain finally converted one of their slew of opportunities. O’Reilly gave the ball away to Olmo on the right flank, Olmo fizzed a pass into Baena and Baena stepped outside a challenge and bent his shot into the corner from the edge of the area. England faded after that and Oyarzabal scored the winner 16 minutes from time, lifting the ball cleverly over Trafford. Spain deserved it. England must resume their forlorn search for their DNA.

Sports.title: How Courtney Lawes FAILED his audition for an England recall: There were great expectations over his return to domestic rugby but he will have to do a lot more to convince Steve Borthwick, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
How Courtney Lawes FAILED his audition for an England recall: There were great expectations over his return to domestic rugby but he will have to do a lot more to convince Steve Borthwick, writes NIK SIMON

This was not what Courtney Lawes had in mind when he traded his life in France.

There were great expectations for the forward's return to English rugby but Sale's opening day at the CorpAcq Stadium did not go to plan.

Alex Sanderson went on a heavy recruitment drive over the summer – Lawes being the headline signing – but it was Bristol's more settled squad that came out on top.

Harry Randall and Louis Rees-Zammit scored two tries apiece for the visitors, who left delighted with their bonus-point victory. 'Very happy', was the summation last night from Bristol coach Pat Lam.

Sale are under pressure to deliver a return on their investment and there are only so many results like this that will be tolerated. Home victories will be key if they are going to make the top four this season.

Ill-discipline gifted Bristol easy entries into the red zone. Lawes spent much of the game trying to put out fires caused by penalties but Bristol's ruck intensity was a notch higher than what he had faced during his two years in France's second division.

There were great expectations for Courtney Lawes' return to English rugby but Sale's opening day did not go to plan

England suddenly have a wealth of locks who can operate at No 6, and Lawes would come in as fifth choice

Sanderson, however, remains supremely confident that his squad will hit the right notes quickly. He said: 'We know there's more in us. We need to improve. We need to be honest and we will be. There are a lot of good players who are going to have better games moving forward.'

There is great debate around whether Lawes will be recalled to the England squad – three years after his last Test – and it will take more than this to convince the national selectors.

Thanks to the rapid development of Alex Coles and the return to fitness of George Martin, England suddenly have a wealth of locks who can operate at No 6. Ollie Chessum is the pick of the bunch and skipper Maro Itoje, who was rested over the summer, must prove that he is still worthy of a place in the starting XV.

Lawes would come in as fifth choice. But head coach Steve Borthwick's move towards a lineout-jumping flanker means Coles, Martin, Chessum and Itoje should all make the matchday 23, meaning Lawes could only be one injury away from a return during the autumn Tests.

When England were selecting their squad for their latest alignment camp, Lawes was listed in the 'maybe' category and Sale must show an all-round improvement if his status is going to change. You suspect he will get there eventually.

Bristol centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg delivered the standout display of the England contenders. He charged down George Ford's channel in the early exchanges, ensuring the No 10 did not have a gentle return to the new season.

It was an underwhelming day for Ford, who dropped the ball inside Bristol's 22 and missed a routine penalty kick to touch. Sale's scrum impressed but their lineout faltered.

There were flashes of energy from Xavier Roe, Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski but Bristol showed more life in the opposition 22. The visitors took the lead after half an hour and the hosts failed to wrestle their way back in front.

Bristol were frustratingly inconsistent last season but Lam believes the workrate on display in Manchester will patch together some of their flaws.

'You want some evidence from the hard work you do in pre-season,' said Lam.

'Ellis Genge spoke on Thursday and said, "I'm ready, I'm confident, let's go". The biggest thing was our work-rate. When we started here 10 years ago, we built our game on being world class at the things that don't require talent. If you get consistency in work-rate, you will get consistency in your attack shape and consistency in your defence shape.

'Too many times last year, we had guys on the ground and guys not in the right places. Our defence and attack wasn't as good last year as it has been and a lot of that comes down to working off the ball.'

The forlorn look on Sanderson's face at the final whistle told a different story to Lam's delight. Ford missed a late penalty that would have scraped a losing bonus point and Sale were left to do some early season soul-searching.

Sports.title: ENGLAND 2-3 SPAIN - PLAYER RATINGS: Which star made too many mistakes? Who had a tough audition? And who will be angry with themselves for not scoring more?
Sports.content:
ENGLAND 2-3 SPAIN - PLAYER RATINGS: Which star made too many mistakes? Who had a tough audition? And who will be angry with themselves for not scoring more?

Spain made it 39 matches unbeaten and counting despite England leading at half-time at Wembley, with defensive errors undoing Thomas Tuchel’s side.

The Three Lions largely had themselves to blame for failing to get something out of this Nations League game as they gifted the ball to the world champions on repeat by their own box.

Marc Guehi gave away possession for their first goal, Nico O’Reilly for their second, and Spain’s third saw them exploit gaps in England’s leaky back line.

Harry Kane will also be frustrated, having squandered a chance to give England a 3-1 lead from the penalty spot, only for a slight slip to see him send the ball crashing into the crossbar.

Here, Daily Mail Sport gave ratings for each and every player for England and Spain.

Spain made it 39 matches unbeaten and counting despite England leading at half-time at Wembley

England (4-2-3-1)

James Trafford – 5

Conceded after 104 seconds to Lamine Yamal, then could not reach Alex Baena’s shot for 2-2 or stop Mikel Oyarzabal for 3-2. Tough audition.

Jarell Quansah – 4

Selected ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, whose passing might have helped with England’s playing from the back. Defence invited danger on themselves over and over.

Ezri Konsa – 5

Konsa was not happy with Quansah after Spain made it 3-2, with the latter having helped them stay onside. England’s back line looked leaky.

Marc Guehi – 3

Wouldn’t get away with this in League Two! Just kidding, but Guehi had to know Yamal was behind him. Not the only mistake he made, either.

Nico O’Reilly – 4

Gave the ball away in the build-up to Spain equalising for 2-2. Almost as if the Manchester City boys were taking turns committing errors.

Elliot Anderson – 5

One early attempt at playing from the back was almost costly as Torres charged through, only to miss the target. Tough evening facing Rodri and Ruiz.

Myles Lewis-Skelly – 5

The Spanish press was suffocating early on, and Lewis-Skelly was one of the culprits seeing his blind passes cut out by Cucurella and Co.

Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham found Barcelona's Anthony Gordon for England's opening goal

Harry Kane headed in for England but smashed his penalty kick against the crossbar after slipping

Bukayo Saka – 5

Trademark left-footed crack after cutting inside from the right just didn’t have enough curl on it to find the corner at 2-2. Limited impact otherwise.

Jude Bellingham – 7

Real Madrid player who assisted a Barcelona player, but it wasn’t for Spain. Pass found Gordon for 1-1. Won the penalty missed by Kane.

Anthony Gordon – 7

He started the move, then he ended it. His flicked lay-off to Bellingham was followed by the burst in behind to score after the one-two.

Harry Kane – 6

Headed in for England’s 2-1 lead. We all thought he would make it 3-1 via his penalty, only to smash the crossbar after slipping. Unfortunate.

Subs

James Garner (for Lewis-Skelly, 69) – 6

Morgan Rogers (for Gordon, 69) – 6

Dominic Calvert-Lewin (for Kane, 83) – N/A

Morgan Gibbs-White (for Saka, 83) – N/A

Jarrad Branthwaite (for Guehi, 89) – N/A

Manager: Thomas Tuchel – 5

That Guehi’s first instinct was to turn backwards towards his goal was not a great look for Tuchel after all the talk of wanting England to be more daring. A costly error which gifted Spain their lead. His side somehow took the lead, but defensive mistakes largely decided this match.

Spain (4-2-3-1)

Unai Simon – 5

Couldn’t stop Gordon when the winger was one-v-one, and won’t thank Cucurella for how he helped Kane’s header bounce beyond him. The unbeaten run continues at least.

Marc Pubill – 6

Eric Garcia was starting, then he withdrew in the warm-up. In came Pubill, tasked with trying to tame Gordon. Hardly an easy ask.

Pau Cubarsi – 6

While England’s defenders were giving away the ball for fun, Spain’s centre backs were far tidier, showing how you should keep possession.

Aymeric Laporte – 6

Perfect punched pass forwards for the goal that gave Spain their 3-2 lead, basically starting an attack from defence.

Marc Cucurella – 5

Kane hardly headed the ball with thunder, but Cucurella froze. He lifted his knee, and only helped deflect it in for England’s 2-1 lead.

Rodri – 6

Told Bellingham to get up, but VAR told the referee to go to his pitch-side monitor. There, he awarded England a penalty for Rodri’s trip.

Rodri gave away a penalty after VAR told the referee to go to his pitch-side monitor

Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal was angry with himself for not scoring more than one

Fabian Ruiz – 5

Had a great view of Gordon as England's winger sprinted in behind Spain. Couldn’t keep up with him. Hardly looked like he even tried to.

Lamine Yamal – 8

Yamal ghosted behind Guehi, stole the ball from him, and made it 1-0. Forever creating chances, even if angry with himself for not scoring more than one.

Dani Olmo – 7

Flashed one chance wide after Yamal’s cute flick found his run into the box. Relentlessly pushed up to the top of the front line to press.

Nico Williams – 4

Tried to do a trick, slipped, lost the ball to Anderson, and just like that, England countered and made it 1-1 via Gordon. His replacement, Baena, was the star man.

Ferran Torres – 4

Gordon did what he could not when one-v-one. Twice the PSG striker only had Trafford to beat, but he failed to finish either chance.

Subs

Alex Baena (for Williams, 55) – 8

Mikel Oyarzabal (for Torres, 55) – 7

Pedri (for Ruiz, 69) – 6

Mikel Merino (for Olmo, 82) – N/A

Manager: Luis De La Fuente – 7

Spain could have led by three goals at half-time. Instead they trailed by one. Funny game, football, though De La Fuente probably wasn’t too pleased. His substitutes led by Alex Baena made sure the reigning world and European champions reached 39 games unbeaten after England gave them a scare.

Fury and Joshua are due to clash in Cardiff on December 11 but their planned face-off next week is set to be scrapped after a row broke out

Tyson Fury claims he is willing to fight David Benavidez if his showdown with Anthony Joshua is cancelled.

Sports.title: Man City verdict LIVE: Chairman breaks silence on 115 charges in new statement
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges of breaching Premier League rules and an appeal is now expected as the football world reacts

Manchester City have been found guilty on 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them in their battle with the Premier League over breaches of financial rules. The verdict from the independent commission has leaked and the football world is working out how to react.

City have always denied the allegations and plan to appeal against the verdict, which covers a nine-year period stretching from 2009 to 2018, meaning that the saga could yet continue for some time. City's hearing against the Premier League took place way back in late 2024.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence," City said in a statement.

Nevertheless, rivals will now be preparing any legal action that they feel appropriate and getting ready to take advantage of whatever situation City may find themselves in.

The commission can impose any punishment they see fit, with points deductions, financial penalties, or even expulsion from the Premier League, all on the table.

Sports.title: Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict

Manchester City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules this week, with calls for the club to issue an apology demanded in the aftermath

View Image Manchester City have been urged to apologise (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Richard Keys has demanded that Manchester City apologise after being found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League financial rules. The Cityzens were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges that they were slapped with in 2023 on Friday.

‌



And while club chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, has urged football fans not to jump to conclusions, continuing to plead innocence, others have called for immediate penalisation and punishment for the infractions. That includes long-time presenter Keys, who most recently worked for BeIN Sports.

‌



Taking to X, the 69-year-old wrote: "The bottom line is Manchester City owe English football an apology. They cheated & warped our game.

‌

"I know it’s nothing to do with the guys on the pitch but most of them wouldn’t have been there if City had played by the rules. Their achievements feel very hollow right now."

Given City's stance on the charges, an appeal of Friday's verdict from an independent panel is expected. As a result, any punishment will not be dished out to the Manchester team until that aspect of the case is concluded.

However, as for the possibilities, the outlook is grim for City. While lighter punishments could come in the form of fines and transfer embargoes, more extreme situations could see the club docked points, expelled from the Premier League or even have their titles won during the affected period - between 2009 and 2018 - stripped.

‌



Any decision is guaranteed to be a little while away as of yet, with fellow Premier League fans and clubs alike set for a period of uncertainty regarding City's situation. For City fans, Al Mubarak has thanked them for their consistent support en-masse.

Sports.title: England pay the penalty in Spain defeat after Harry Kane's miss - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
England pay the penalty in Spain defeat after Harry Kane's miss - 5 talking points

ENGLAND 2-3 SPAIN: Harry Kane missed a penalty as Thomas Tuchel's side were beaten in their Nations League opener, having led until the hour mark against the newly crowned world champions

View 5 Images Harry Kane missed a penalty with England leading (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

England were left ruing a rare Harry Kane penalty miss as they came out on the wrong end of a five-goal thriller against Spain. Thomas Tuchel's side lost 3-2 at Wembley in their first game since the World Cup.

‌



Lamine Yamal put Spain ahead inside two minutes, punishing Marc Guehi's mistake. But England hit back with two goals before half-time courtesy of Anthony Gordon and Kane.

‌



Early in the second half, Kane was given the chance to put the Three Lions two goals to the good but missed his penalty. Alex Baena equalised six minutes later before the world champions won it through Mikel Oyarzabal and claimed all three points in this Nations League clash.

‌



Here are five talking points from Wembley.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



1. Trafford in - but not for long

One major surprise on the team sheet: James Trafford started in goal ahead of Jordan Pickford. The Leeds shot-stopper has had an excellent start to the season and was handed his first competitive cap by Thomas Tuchel.

And the England manager confirmed before kick-off that Trafford will keep his place for Tuesday's game away to Czechia before Pickford returns for the Three Lions' final two fixtures during this extended international break. It's set to be a battle for the gloves with an eye on Euro 2028.

Should James Trafford be England's No.1? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images James Trafford and Jordan Pickford will each play two games (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

2. Guehi's gift for Yamal

"Keep it tight, lads. Nothing silly." That's the message that will've been echoed around dressing rooms across England at 2:55pm on Saturday - but Marc Guehi didn't get the memo.

The Manchester City centre-back turned on the ball 25 yards from goal and had his pocket picked by Lamine Yamal, who cooly finished past Trafford with two minutes on the clock. It was an uncharacteristic error from one of England's most reliable players and gave the Three Lions an even greater task against the world champions.

‌



View 5 Images Lamine Yamal punished Marc Guehi for his mistake (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

3. The English DNA on show

Anthony Gordon said this week that England should stop trying to play like Spain because it's not in their DNA. So what is?

For starters, counter attacks. A slip from Nico Williams allowed England to break away from the edge of their own boss, as Gordon and Jude Bellingham combined to equalise.

‌



It started with Gordon's backheel to Bellingham, allowing the Real Madrid midfielder to drive forward down the centre of the pitch. His pass was perfectly weighted for Gordon, who had pace to burn and ice in his veins to slot the ball past Unai Simon.

Secondly in the DNA test, you'd find headed goals. England had their tails up after Gordon's goal and shortly after firing a shot narrowly wide, Harry Kane nodded in Nico O'Reilly's cross courtesy of a deflection from Marc Cucurella.

Their captain's goal gave England the lead at half-time. Spain must've been kicking themselves, having missed a series of chances through Ferran Torres and Dani Olmo.

‌



View 5 Images Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon turned the game on its head (Image: Matt Lewis - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

4. Kane pays the penalty

His miss against France in Qatar may still be burned into England fans' memories, but Kane not scoring from the penalty spot is still a rare sight in football. But we saw it again when, following a VAR check, Rodri was deemed to have brought down Bellingham before the hour mark.

Kane stepped up and went high, rattling Simon's crossbar. It turned out that the Bayern Munich striker had touched the ball with his standing foot, potentially explaining why his effort crashed the bar to keep the game wide open.

‌



It didn't take long for Kane to be punished. When a stray pass from O'Reilly was pounced on by Olmo, the ball made its way to Alex Baena on the edge of England's penalty area, and the substitute produced a superb finish to level the scores in the 60th minute.

View 5 Images Alex Baena equalised for Spain after Harry Kane's miss (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

5. Oyarzabal's hot streak continues

No goals in eight games for Real Sociedad this season but 18 in his last 20 for Spain. Mikel Oyarzabal loves scoring for his country.

Article continues below

Left out of the starting XI in favour of Ferran, Oyarzabal reminded Luis de la Fuente of how clinical he is with another crucial strike - just like his one against England in the Euro 2024 final. England were cut open by Aymeric Laporte as the ball was fizzed into Baena, who showed brilliant composure to turn and thread his team-mate in on goal.

The Three Lions' defence was scrambled by the slick build-up play and Oyarzabal calmly dinked the ball over Trafford to restore Spain's lead. England rallied for an equaliser but burnout had set in, as they started their Nations League campaign with a defeat.

Sports.title: Hidden message offers hope Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will go ahead
Sports.content:
Hidden message offers hope Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will go ahead

Fury and Joshua are due to clash in the early hours of December 12 in Cardiff following an announcement last week - but several issues remain unresolved

View Image Tyson Fury and AJ will clash in Cardiff later this year (Image: Getty)

Dana White's role in Tyson Fury's showdown with Anthony Joshua has been downplayed after Fury claimed the fight was in jeopardy.

‌



Fury and Joshua are due to clash in the early hours of December 12 in Cardiff following an announcement last week. But a planned press conference and face-off next week is now in doubt after Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn insisted a number of issues remain outstanding.

‌



Among those are when Fury is due to begin drug testing, and the role of UFC CEO White who has long claimed to be the promoter of the fight. He was mentioned on the official announcement last week, leading Hearn to double down on his insistence that White is contractually not allowed to be involved.

‌



That led to Fury claiming Joshua is ready to pull out of the fight, but during the broadcast of White's Zuffa Boxing show in London on Saturday night, commentator Max Kellerman said: "Dana White's involvement in the fight, so people know, is purely in assisting Turki Alalshikh, who has been the engine behind just about every big fight in boxing over the last handful of years. He's assisting Turki in a personal capacity, not as a promoter."

The 3 major issues threatening Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at risk of collapse after new contract row READ MORE :

Kellerman's claim appears to be an olive branch to Hearn who has had an ongoing feud with White ever since the American launched his promotion and swooped to sign Conor Benn who had been with Hearn since turning professional a decade ago. But it remains to be seen whether Joshua and Fury will fly in from their training camps in Dubai and Miami respectively this week.

‌



On Friday night, Fury took to social media to accuse his rival of putting the fight at risk of collapse. “Breaking news. Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight," he said. "They’re saying they’re not gonna fight now. They’re little s******** cowards.

“It’s mainly to do with Eddie Hearn’s ego. He’s making up a million different things and threatening ‘we’re not gonna fight, we’re not gonna fight, we’re not gonna fight’. He’s cost us the biggest fight in boxing history. Clown.” Multiple attempts to arrange the highest grossing event in British boxing history have failed, most notably in 2021 when Deontay Wilder used arbitration to force a trilogy fight with Fury when the ‘Gypsy King’ had a signed contract with Joshua.

Months of wrangling that saw Croke Park, Wembley, Madison Square Garden and then the successful venue of Cardiff’s Principality Stadium come into contention for the latest attempt to resurrect their meeting finally appeared on Thursday. Fury has suggested that alternative opponents to Joshua are now being lined up for him.

Article continues below

He said: “AJ, pull your finger out you little white-flagged, yellow-bellied coward. Now I’m coming home. The Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdom to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales, you absolute little nugget, bodybuilding sausage.

“Now you’re making a million excuses. Now you’ve got Turki Alalshikh finding alternative real men who will fight at the drop of a hat. So I hope yous are happy, you little cowardly b*******. I’ve never seen anything like you. You’re pure s********** and this is mainly to do with Eddie Hearn’s ego. What a little p****.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane and Ian Wright urge Premier League to punish Man City after 'cheat' verdict
Sports.content:
Roy Keane and Ian Wright urge Premier League to punish Man City after 'cheat' verdict

Ian Wright and Roy Keane were on hand to give their opinion on Manchester City's Premier League charges guilty verdict during ITV's coverage of the Nations League

View Image Roy Keane and Ian Wright agree about Manchester City's charges (Image: ITV)

Roy Keane and Ian Wright agree that Manchester City should be severely punished for 'cheating' after being found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Following a long and drawn-out three year saga, an independent panel found City guilty of all but one of the 115 charges slapped against them by English top flight officials on Friday evening.

‌



While City are expected to appeal the decision, given they have continually plead their innocence, the footballing world was sent into a frenzy by the earth-shattering news, with players, pundits and fans all having their say. Highlighting the extent of the controversy, Rodri spent a large portion of his Nations League press conference for Spain answering questions regarding his former club's alleged wrongdoing.

‌



And now, Premier League legends Keane and Wright have given their verdict on matters. Speaking during ITV's coverage of the Nations League clash between England and Spain at Wembley alongside Mark Pougatch and Juan Mata, Keane said: "Well it's about time [the decision was made]. It's obviously been going on a long time now and I certainly would disagree with Rodri's messages there.

‌

"It was the choice of the club, they chose to cheat, and whatever they have won over the last few years, they deserve to be punished. Where we start and finish with that, obviously it's difficult.

"But they were cheating. Been found guilty of it, they have to take their medicine now. And it was kind of a shock really to be found guilty of...114 of the charges they were found guilty of? Big news it was."

When asked where the debacle leaves the reputation of English football, Wright then added: "Not very good, not very good. I'm going to be totally honest, Pougs.

‌



"Going back to Rodri, he's talking about what he's done. He went shoulder to shoulder with the guys, and, of course, you can't take that away from them, they experienced that.

Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023 (also below). Every word matters and holds true. While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed.

Article continues below

"We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.

"We have some exciting moments to look forward to after this international break. We travel to Anfield in a fortnight, and then host Paris St Germain in the Champions League back at Etihad Stadium - moments that give us an opportunity to celebrate the strength of the Manchester City family. Thank you, as always, for your constant support."
