World.title: Mbappe out for two weeks or more with knee injury say Real
World.content:
Paris – France captain Kylian Mbappe suffered a hyperextension of his left knee playing for France, his club Real Madrid said Saturday but could be ready to play again when La Liga resumes.

“Following tests carried out today by Real Madrid’s medical department on our player Kylian Mbappe, he has been diagnosed with a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee,” the Spanish club said in a statement.

The forward left the pitch shortly after opening the scoring in a 1-0 French win against Turkey on Friday.

New France coach Zinedine Zidane said France were “not going to take any risks” and that he would not use Mbappe in the three Nations League matches scheduled over the next 10 days.

France travel to Belgium on Monday before hosting Italy and Belgium at the Stade de France on October 2 and 5.

Real Madrid’s first game after the international break, with Villarreal on October 10, might be too soon for an Mbappe return but Spanish daily AS reported Saturday he would ceratinly be ready for the Classico with Barcelona October 25.

World.title: Iraq beats Kuwait 3-2 in Gulf Cup thriller with dramatic late winner
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq claimed their first victory of the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup with a thrilling 3-2 win over Kuwait on Saturday at the Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Stadium in Jeddah, as substitute Karrar Nabeel struck a thunderous stoppage-time winner to settle a dramatic encounter between the two Gulf rivals.

After opening their Group A campaign with a 1-1 draw against Oman, Iraq needed a win in Kuwait and got one in dramatic manner, with coach Graham Arnold’s changes transforming the final moments.

Following a goalless first half, Zidane Iqbal put Iraq ahead in the 52nd minute, giving the Lions of Mesopotamia the breakthrough after starting the match in midfield.

Kuwait equalized in the 75th minute when Yousef Nasser scored from the penalty spot, setting up a tense final 15 minutes.

Iraq reclaimed the lead eight minutes later when Saif Rashid scored a fantastic acrobatic goal from a cross to make it 2-1.

As the game progressed, Arnold’s replacements added new energy to Iraq’s offensive.

Jussef Nasrawe shined after coming on, giving speed and direct running down the right flank while regularly putting pressure on Kuwait’s defense.

Karrar Nabeel also came off the bench and would later provide a crucial contribution.

Kuwait refused to give up, as Nasser scored again in the 90th minute to complete his brace and tie the game at 2-2, seemingly winning his team a point.

Iraq replied nearly instantly.

Nabeel fired a tremendous shot deep into stoppage time to make it 3-2, igniting jubilation among Iraqi players and fans and capping off an incredible encounter.

The contribution from Iraq’s bench was especially significant.

Nasrawe provided Iraq with additional offensive danger down the right, and Nabeel’s entrance resulted in the game-winning goal.

Iraq now has four points from their first two Group A matches, after a tie with Oman in which Mohammed Qasim scored the only goal.

Saturday’s success also extended Iraq’s current undefeated streak against Kuwait, who last defeated the Iraqi national team in 2014.

The match brought another unforgettable chapter to one of Gulf football’s long-standing rivalries.

Kuwait is the competition’s most successful country, with ten trophies, while Iraq has won the Gulf Cup four times, most recently in Basra in 2023.

The style of Iraq’s victory offered an added boost: Iqbal scored the first goal, Saif scored a fantastic second, Nasrawe helped fuel the assault from the bench, and Nabeel scored the winner at the end.

Iraq will now focus on their last Group A encounter against Saudi Arabia on September 29, with Arnold’s team aiming for a spot in the Gulf Cup semifinals.

World.title: At least 16 killed in Russian and Ukrainian strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 16 people over the last 24 hours, both countries said Saturday, with the war still raging in its fifth year.

Both Moscow and Kyiv have stepped up attacks after the deadliest summer since 2022 — the year Russia launched its invasion, starting Europe’s worst war since World War Two.

US-led talks to end fighting have not led to a breakthrough and the Kremlin has repeatedly said it intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine.

Kyiv said Russian strikes had killed at least six people — in northeastern Sumy, in Zaporizhzhia and in the Dnipropetrovsk region, where a 17-year-old girl was among the victims.

And in Kyiv, several people were wounded a day after a day-time Russian attack killed seven people. Moscow has intensified strikes on the capital as the city prepares for another winter of war.

Russia said Ukrainian strikes had killed four people in its Krasnodar and Belgorod regions.

Vladimir Saldo, appointed by Moscow to lead occupational authorities in the Kherson region, said a Ukrainian drone had hit a cafe in the village of Askaniya-Nova, near Crimea, Friday evening.

“Under the rubble, rescuers found the bodies of two young girls — born in 2004 and 2006,” he said on Telegram, adding that a man had also been killed in the same area.

Moscow-appointed official Yevgeny Balitsky said night-time Ukrainian strikes killed three more people in the occupied part of the Zaporizhzhia region.

United Nations officials have warned about the increasing numbers of civilian victims in the war.

At the UN General Assembly this week, US President Donald Trump once again said that a deal between Moscow and Kyiv to end the war was “going to happen”.*

For many observers however, that prospect appeared distant.

– ‘Everything is burning’ –

Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday that Russia was “escalating every single day”.

In Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district, residents of a typical Soviet-era apartment bock hit by a Russian drone were cleaning up their building — already worried about what might come next.

Oleksandr Gorlachov, 43, had gone to his allotment plot outside the city Friday night.

Early Saturday morning however, he was woken up by a video call from his elderly parents — who are both deaf — and rushed back to help.

“I watched as my mother is standing there in her nightgown, my father in his underwear, outside the building in tears… and there are flames, everything is burning,” he told AFP.

“The apartment is completely smashed up.”

His mother, he said, is a seamstress.

“Her sewing machine was there. She was in tears because it’s broken now. So, well, it’s a tragedy. But in my family everyone is alive and for that I thank God,” he said.

With mounting Russian attacks on the capital, his family is in “constant stress” and he tries to distract himself by planting tomatoes.

“They don’t have enough land,” he said, mocking Russia — the world’s largest country. “They want to simply wipe out our nation.”

– ‘Not going anywhere’ –

Despite Russia making life in Kyiv increasingly tough, Gorlachov said he “wasn’t going anywhere”.

But fellow resident Anastasiia Grygorovych — woken up when her window “fell on me” — had already fled her home-town of Gorlivka, now occupied by Russia.

Now she was considering leaving Ukraine altogether.

“In general, I’m already thinking that I need to leave,” she said.

Russia’s invasion has forced millions to flee their homes.

Kyiv also hit Russia with retaliatory strikes Saturday. Ukraine has struck deeper inside Russia this year, hitting as far as the Urals and Siberia.

Zelensky said Kyiv hit an oil refinery in the southern Russian Krasnodar region and a plant “supplying the occupiers” in the neighbouring Rostov region.

The Ukrainian leader called on allies to adopt more sanctions on Moscow.

World.title: Russell holds off Verstappen to claim imperious victory in Baku
World.content:
Baku – George Russell resisted a late charge from Max Verstappen to claim his first lights-to-flag victory with a composed drive for Mercedes in Saturday’s thrilling Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old Briton came home just 0.196 seconds ahead of the four-time champion with his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar third on his return after a broken wrist in a race punctuated by two safety cars.

It was Russell’s first win on the fast, challenging streets of Baku, his first since the Austrian Grand Prix in June,and the eighth of his career. It trimmed team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ championship to 66 points.

Antonelli finished fifth behind Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc after slicing through the field from 16th on the grid. Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton was sixth in the second Ferrari.

“It’s amazing to be back on the top step so I want to say a big thank you to the team for helping me through a tough moment,” said Russell.

“The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing, getting the gap, but after the safety car I saw Max behind me and I knew it wasn’t going to be easy.

“When the yellow flag came out, I lifted off the power and when I came back I had no turbo and Max nearly got me on the line.”

Verstappen was philosophical.

“We had a good race,” he said. “In the final lap, George lost a bit of boost so that’s why I caught up quite a bit. It got close, but it wasn’t enough.”

Hadjar drove in pain.

“It’s been a very long six weeks since I injured myself, but it felt like the right moment to come back. I felt strong and this is my first proper podium finish on pure pace so I am delighted.”

Racing Bulls’ rookie Arvid Lindblad was seventh, Esteban Ocon eighth ahead of his Haas team-mate Oliver Bearman and Williams’ Carlos Sainz.

Russell made a near-perfect start from his 12th pole position to draw clear while, behind him, Oscar Piastri took advantage of a slow-starting Leclerc to take second. Antonelli dropped from 16th to 17th.

Verstappen also enjoyed the opening lap and passed both Alpines before powering past Hamilton, Norris, Leclerc and finally team-mate Hadjar to rise to third.

The Dutchman was grumbling about his tyres, but Russell on the same medium compound was already five seconds ahead of Piastri on softs.

By mid-distance, Russell led by 10 seconds, but grazed the wall at Turn 15.

– ‘Oh my God! Oh my God!’ –

Team-mate Antonelli was up to ninth as the Red Bulls scrapped for third, making life easy for Piastri in second.

The processional action ended on lap 30 when Williams’ Alex Albon crashed at Turn Five, triggering a Safety Car deployment during which the leaders all pitted.

After five laps, the race resumed with the Dutchman passing Piastri at Turn One .

Behind him Franco Colapinto lunged up the inside but ran out of space entering the next corner. He locked up and went sideways pushing Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly into Lando Norris in a McLaren. The three went off the track in a synchronised slide.

Both drivers for the struggling French team were in position for top-10 finishes.

“Oh my God! Oh my God! I don’t believe it,” said Gasly on team radio adding a swear word. “So many points gone.”

A second safety car came out for three laps. After the restart Piastri locked-up,dropping to 14th and gifting Hadjar third.

Antonelli passed Hamilton with 10 laps to go to take fifth.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi meets UN High Commissioner for Refugees Barham Salih in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi met with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Barham Salih, and his accompanying delegation in New York to evaluate the status of refugees and internally displaced persons (IDPs), alongside joint humanitarian relief programs.

The diplomatic discussions were held on the sidelines of Al-Zaidi’s active participation in the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The talks centered on deepening institutional coordination between the Iraqi Federal Government and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), with a particular focus on mobilizing technical resources and international assistance to support vulnerable displaced populations.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi underscored that Baghdad places human rights and humanitarian protection at the forefront of its national priorities, maintaining consistent cooperation with the UNHCR and relevant multilateral agencies to enhance living conditions, deliver targeted welfare services, and rebuild stability across liberated and crisis-impacted areas.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the necessity of tackling the root causes driving involuntary displacement and asylum seeking, calling for cohesive regional and international coordination frameworks to safeguard the fundamental rights of displaced groups in strict alignment with international conventions and statutory humanitarian laws.

In response, High Commissioner Salih confirmed the agency’s commitment to supporting Iraq through comprehensive relief and developmental operations, stressing that the UNHCR will continue working with Baghdad to fulfill all operational and financial benchmarks necessary to permanently resolve the internal displacement file.

World.title: PM Al-Zaidi asserts state monopoly on arms and outlines economic vision at UNGA81
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi delivered a wide-ranging policy address before the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, presenting Baghdad’s strategic vision for national sovereignty, economic restructuring, and regional stability.

Reaffirming Iraq’s adherence to the principles of the United Nations Charter, Al-Zaidi framed the nation as an ascending economic force and an essential bridge for multilateral dialogue and cooperative diplomacy. He declared that the country’s immediate priorities stem from a decisive national will to restore the prestige of the rule of law, consolidate constitutional governance, and rebuild public confidence in sovereign state institutions.

Addressing the nation’s security architecture, the Prime Minister emphasized that the federal government holds the exclusive authority to determine matters of peace and war, asserting that all arms and instruments of legitimate force must remain strictly confined to the command of constitutional institutions.

Al-Zaidi underscored that current executive and regulatory enforcement measures are rooted in statutory mandates and supreme national interest, aimed at defending territorial integrity, consolidating security gains, and establishing the stable environment required to support sustainable socio-economic development and incoming international investments.

Highlighting a pivotal sovereign transition, Al-Zaidi noted that the conclusion of the U.S.-led International Coalition’s mission in Iraq marks a strategic evolution in Baghdad’s foreign partnerships, pivoting defense-centric alignments toward multifaceted economic and developmental cooperation.

He stressed that Iraqi forces have built the requisite autonomous military and intelligence capabilities to defend the nation’s borders, land, and people in the post-defeat era of terrorism. To sustain this regional equilibrium, the Prime Minister called on international partners and neighboring states to enforce rigorous border management, eliminate security gaps, and maintain constant counter-extremism coordination.

Turning to economic governance, Al-Zaidi outlined Iraq’s ongoing campaign against administrative and financial corruption, identifying the recovery and safeguarding of public funds as an indispensable pillar of institutional reform. He articulated an ambitious modernization agenda designed to transition Iraq away from the vulnerabilities of a rentier economy toward a dynamic, open-market framework integrated with global digital and technological systems.

To realize this transition, the federal government has established legal, tax, and customs incentives aimed at empowering private enterprises, attracting foreign direct investment, and leveraging Iraq’s strategic geographical crossroads to expand commercial flows.

In the energy sector, the Prime Minister reaffirmed comprehensive plans to boost crude oil production, capture and process natural gas reserves, and scale up refining capacities alongside downstream petrochemical industries, aiming to cement Iraq’s standing as a dependable global energy supplier.

Al-Zaidi voiced grave concern regarding disruptions to freedom of navigation and commercial shipping routes that have triggered sharp increases in global energy prices. To insulate national revenues and reinforce global market stability, he confirmed that Baghdad is actively advancing strategic pipeline corridors linking Iraq with Turkey, Jordan, and Syria to diversify crude export outlets away from maritime chokepoints.

Concluding his address, the Prime Minister presented Iraq’s multibillion-dollar Development Road project as an overarching blueprint for regional integration, characterizing the multimodal transit corridor as a vital artery connecting East and West through trade, logistics, industry, and energy networks.

Finally, Al-Zaidi invited neighboring states and global investment partners to participate directly in the transit corridor, reiterating Iraq’s conviction that shared economic interests, reciprocal trade ties, and cross-border infrastructure constitute the most durable foundation for lasting regional peace and prosperity.

World.title: Basra tribesmen liberate hijacked oil tanker in Gulf of Aden
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A tribal dignitary from Basra Governorate revealed on Friday, September 25, 2026, that approximately 40 members of the Al-Shaghanba tribe from the Abu Al-Khaseeb district successfully liberated a hijacked crude oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden, freeing the crew and capturing seven armed pirates.

Sheikh Ali Al-Shaghanbi stated that the commercial vessel, owned by an Iraqi businessman belonging to the Al-Shaghanba tribe, was intercepted and boarded by maritime pirates while transiting strategic maritime lanes off the southern Arabian Peninsula.

According to the tribal leader, the pirates seized control of the tanker, took the crew hostage, and issued ransom demands as a condition for their release.

In response, an expeditionary group of roughly 40 armed tribesmen from Abu Al-Khaseeb and the village of Jaykoor mobilized to mount a direct recovery operation, coordinating logistics and tracking through international contacts positioned outside Iraq.

The intervention concluded with the tribal forces successfully storming the vessel, regaining full command of the tanker, and securing the safe release of all detained crew members unharmed.

Sheikh Al-Shaghanbi confirmed that the clash resulted in the capture and detention of seven armed pirates found aboard the vessel, while remaining members of the pirate group managed to flee the maritime perimeter.

World.title: Al Zaidi courts US banks in New York targeting 10M bpd oil capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Under the auspices and in the presence of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Iraq to the United Nations in New York hosted a high-level roundtable meeting bringing together representatives from premier American commercial banks and financial institutions, Iraqi banking delegates, senior government officials, and economic analysts.

Held late Thursday evening Baghdad time on September 24, 2026, the diplomatic engagement was convened to re-establish institutional communication between Iraq’s financial sector and the international banking architecture, with a particular focus on direct correspondent relationships with major U.S. lenders.

In his address to the executive gathering, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi stressed that Iraq has embarked on an irreversible trajectory of structural economic transformation and banking sector modernization. He acknowledged that past vulnerabilities within Iraq’s domestic banking ecosystem were partly rooted in institutional isolation and restricted interaction with global financial hubs, particularly American banking conglomerates.

Al-Zaidi extended an open invitation to U.S. financial institutions to establish direct operational footprints in the Iraqi market, emphasizing that their market entry would represent a qualitative leap toward elevating local banking practices, adopting international compliance standards, and deepening Iraq’s integration into global capital networks.

Highlighting Iraq’s macroeconomic foundations, the Prime Minister noted that the country currently produces approximately 4.5 million barrels of crude oil per day, with federal energy policies actively targeting an expansion toward 10 million barrels per day over the long term.

This hydrocarbon expansion strategy is designed to maximize sovereign revenues and channel critical liquidity into national development, industrial manufacturing, and cross-sector economic diversification. Al-Zaidi assured participants that the government is actively engineering an investor-friendly environment with streamlined regulatory, customs, and fiscal frameworks, underscoring that American banks hold vast opportunities to structure project financing, issue commercial credit, and underwrite major capital ventures across energy, logistics, and real estate.

Detailing administrative reforms underway, Al-Zaidi outlined the government’s clear operational blueprint for comprehensive institutional restructuring across state-owned commercial banks. The initiative aims to enforce corporate governance benchmarks, upgrade anti-money laundering and know-your-customer compliance mechanisms, and build an agile banking framework capable of supporting modern commercial activities.

The Prime Minister affirmed that statutory anti-corruption proceedings, asset recovery drives, and fiscal protection measures are advancing effectively, reiterating Baghdad’s commitment to institutional transparency and the safeguarding of public and private investment funds.

World.title: 2 more Naga men killed as ethnic violence flares up in Manipur again
World.content:
Manipur violence claims another life as gunmen strike Senapati village

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.The shooting took place under Senapati police station around 2.30pm, shortly after CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh left a function about 30km away. It came two days after four Tangkhul Naga men were killed allegedly by Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma (B) at Pilong village near the international border in Kamjong district.The Kalenjang and Pilong killings are part of a series of Naga-Kuki clashes that began in Feb, shortly after Singh's govt took charge. At least 21 people - 11 Nagas and 10 Kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since Aug 27. The toll is separate from the Meitei-Kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.Both the communities have accused militant groups from the other side of the attacks. Police have said several such allegations are under investigation and have not been independently verified.The killings came as United Naga Council (UNC), the apex body of Naga tribes in Manipur, called off its 131-day economic blockade of NH-2 and NH-37 after a meeting with home ministry and Manipur govt at the BSF Frontier headquarters in Guwahati Saturday.The blockade followed the abduction of six Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi district.Manipur Congress president Okram Ibobi Singh accused BJP-headed NDA govts in the state and Centre of remaining "silent spectators" to civilian killings. "Govt is behaving as if it is not concerned about the killings of civilians of any community," the former three-time CM said. "We strongly condemn the killings of innocent civilians from Naga, Kuki and Meitei communities," he said, while questioning security along the Myanmar border.

World.title: India's right to defend itself from terrorism will be exercised: EAM
World.content:
EAM S Jaishankar

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Describing Pakistan as a serial practitioner of terrorism in his UNGA address, foreign minister S Jaishankar said that there must be no dilution of the zero-tolerance approach to the menace. Without naming Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, who had raked up the Kashmir issue in his General Assembly speech on Friday, Jaishankar said he had misrepresented facts and invoked arguments to normalise terrorism and claim immunity from its consequences."That will not stand," said the minister, adding that the scourge of terrorism had been a persistent threat to peace.Jaishankar called state-sponsored terrorism with a cross-border purpose a direct challenge to the global order, adding that India's right to defend itself from terrorism will be exercised.In his remarks, Sharif had yet again given credit to US President Donald Trump for ending the India-Pakistan conflict last year with his "timely intervention"."Govts indulging in such practices must be held accountable. There must be no dilution in our zero-tolerance approach towards terrorism. Its financial aspects, in particular, should be exposed and should be countered," said Jaishankar."Friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism.And understandings premised on that will naturally be called into question. It is for the perpetrator of terrorism to mend its ways," he added.He also flagged the need to end conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine, saying the inability to maintain peace is not just undermining security but threatening progress and retarding development. "In a globalised world, the effects of war are felt worldwide. Countries far from conflicts are being penalised for no fault of theirs. Those most impacted often have the least say.""The targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers transiting international waterways is simply unacceptable," he said. Speaking on the West Asia crisis, the minister backed the two-state solution for durable and lasting peace.Jaishankar spoke about the Global South predicament in today's world and also the misuse of AI. He said a mindset of extreme competition had set in, undermining institutions and establishing choke points."Global South's right to industrialise is also undermined by non-market practices and market denial. The march of technology that was meant to instill hope has now become a source of anxiety. Misuse of AI is sharpening bias and diluting mutual respect. These directions bode ill for the aims and objectives of the UN."

World.title: Higher EPF wage limit: Monthly PF contributions rise to Rs 3,917
World.content:
EPFO wage ceiling hike

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With EPFO increasing the mandatory wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 a month to Rs 25,000, employees will now contribute Rs 3,000 (at 12% contribution of Rs 25,000 wage) towards their PF savings from Rs 1,800 earlier, govt said in a set of FAQs released. This will be along with a contribution of Rs 917 by employers (at 3.67%), up from Rs 550, taking the mandatory monthly PF contributions to Rs 3,917.In addition, Rs 2,083 - an 8.3% contribution from employers' share - will now go towards the pension kitty from earlier Rs 1,250. On Sept 17, govt increased EPFO wage ceiling to bring one crore additional workers into the social security net as minimum wages in at least seven states and UTs - Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand - have crossed the Rs 15,000 threshold.In the case of an employee with a monthly wage of Rs 20,000, the mandatory PF contribution will be Rs 3,134 - the employee share Rs 2,400 and the employer share Rs 734, with an additional Rs 1,666 going towards EPS from employer's share. But if an employee earns, say, Rs 35,000 a month, the mandatory PF contribution will be Rs 6,000 (Rs 3,000 from employee and employers each), with no amount going towards pension as EPS is available only to those whose wages do not exceed the EPFO wage ceiling.The retirement savings agency said the new regime kicked in from Sept 17 and asked employers to review contractor compliance, wherever contract labour is engaged, and update its payroll systems.Allaying employee fears of attempts to pass on the contribution by deducting more from salaries, it said an employer's statutory contribution cannot simply be treated as an employee deduction merely by describing it as part of CTC.While the move will likely increase compliance costs for small and medium enterprises, the potential costs due to the rise in the wage ceiling can be partly offset by the incentive of up to Rs 3,000 per month for every additional employment created under PM Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana.

World.title: BJP allies close ranks, flay opposition for 'undermining democracy'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP's allies on Saturday closed ranks to hit out at opposition, with TDP chief and Andhra Pradesh CM

saying EC's statement reaffirmed "the integrity and credibility of our constitutional institutions" and ended "misconceptions" around it.

"Attempts to undermine global confidence in India's democratic framework for short-term political gains are deeply unfortunate," he said, urging opposition to accept wins and losses with grace.

LJP (Ram Vilas)'s Chirag Paswan said opposition is spreading confusion and questioned why it keeps silent on states where it has formed govt.

JDU member Sanjay Jha said rising frustration over poll defeats have led opposition to spread propaganda to undermine the democracy.

Shiv Sena's Eknath Shinde said Congress keeps mum when it wins but attacks EC when it loses. The united stand came a day after some allies had pressed EC to clarify concerns raised in media reports.

World.title: Congress owes nation a public apology: Nabin after EC statement
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the

's statement,

Saturday said it has exposed

and its allies as their attack on the poll body was nothing but a continuation of their tactic of shifting blame for their shrinking popular support in elections and demanded their apology.

BJP president

Nitin Nabin

said, "Opposition has once again been exposed for misleading the public on SIR. EC has made it clear that every decision relating to the SIR was taken unanimously by the full commission. Yet, Congress chose to build its allegations around a manufactured lie and attack our constitutional bodies."

Today, their web of lies stands exposed yet again," Prasad said.

He claimed that the EC statement has made it clear that the Indian Express story was "factually incorrect".

World.title: INDIA bloc to meet on Sept 30, CEC's ouster on top of agenda
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Opposition INDIA bloc will meet on Sept 30 to discuss the alleged manipulation of poll rolls under SIR and a possible joint struggle to press for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

The meeting has been scheduled against the backdrop of nationwide outrage triggered by revelations that ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had questioned many of the decisions regarding SIR.

The opposition, led by Rahul Gandhi, has said the revelations tie in with their allegations of 'vote chori' in favour of BJP over the last two years. It has demanded the scrapping of the SIR process.

TMC MP Derek O'Brien said the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation is "non-negotiable", while other issues will also be discussed at the meeting.

"We will work unitedly and purposefully."

The meeting is expected to be attended by the leading lights of the anti-BJP front, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Uddhav Thackeray and MA Baby.

The meeting has been scheduled after CPM's MA Baby wrote to parties (including AAP, DMK and CJP) seeking an immediate meeting.

Trinamool's Mamata Banerjee also reached out to INDIA bloc members.





She called the CEC "Vanish Kumar", demanded his ouster and said the Bengal mandate was stolen.

The joint brainstorming will follow a Congress Working Committee meet on Sept 29.

The parties are also planning to submit a fresh "removal notice" against Kumar in both Houses of Parliament.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

CPI-ML's Dipankar Bhattacharya said that there is a strong belief within INDIA bloc that some parties (Aam Aadmi Party and DMK) which are not part of the alliance umbrella should also be roped in to boost the campaign.

It also released a fact-finding report regarding SIR in constituencies that the party lost narrowly in recent Bihar assembly polls and claimed it found 17-25% of voters had been wrongly deleted.

The meeting assumes special significance as Cockroach Janata Party and other youth outfits have already announced a stir over the issue.

CJP has reiterated that it will launch a nationwide agitation from Mumbai on Oct 2 after its ultimatum seeking the resignation of Kumar ended Saturday. Azad Maidan is most likely to be the venue of its protest.

World.title: PM Modi gave energy access to more than anyone in history: Aus PM
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has credited PM

with providing energy access to India's population on a scale that, he said, no other country has achieved before.

Speaking at an event on Sept 24 organised by Asia Policy Institute in New York on the sidelines of UNGA meetings, he said, "To give PM Modi credit, more people have been connected with access to energy in India under his reign than has occurred in any decade in any country or any region in human history."

Under the Ujjwala scheme, over 10.5 crore cooking gas connections have been provided since 2016, while the Saubhagya scheme helped electrify over 2.8 crore rural and poor urban households. The PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana has connected over 50 lakh households with solar energy.

Albanese is likely to visit India in Dec when bilateral trade and cooperation in clean energy are expected to be discussed.

World.title: India, Bangladesh look towards Rahman visit in Nov
World.content:
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman

NEW DELHI: After an earlier attempt was aborted, India and Bangladesh are looking to schedule a visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India in the third week of Nov, sources said.Efforts to reschedule the visit are likely to gain momentum after the arrival of the new Bangladesh high commissioner, Asad Alam Siam, in the last week of Oct or early Nov. For Dhaka though, the key concern - one which might decide whether the visit materialises - is the unresolved issue of former PM Hasina's extradition.Rahman's birthday greetings to Modi and the latter's prompt response seem to have boosted the likelihood of an early finalisation of dates for the visit. However, neither side has confirmed - or denied - reports that NSA Ajit Doval travelled to Dhaka recently. The 'visit' was reported to have taken place on Sept 17.

World.title: Bihar CM bats for coordination between centre and State to curb infiltration in border areas of Nepal
World.content:
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday (September 26, 2026) said that the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Bihar Police, and central agencies should work in coordination to bolster security along the India-Nepal border.

Mr. Choudhary said this during a high-level review meeting regarding various issues concerning the India-Nepal border. Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai and Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary were also present in the meeting.

Detailed presentations were made on border security, border management, law and order in border areas, and the prevention of illegal activities.

During the review meeting, Mr. Choudhary said that the security of India is a top responsibility and, given the sensitivity of the India-Nepal border, security and management systems should be continuously strengthened.

“The SSB, Bihar Police, and central agencies must work in coordination to ensure effective control over any form of illegal activity in the border region,”Mr. Choudhary said.

He directed that special vigilance be maintained against infiltration, the use of forged documents, counterfeit currency, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities in the border areas.

“Ensure the availability of machines for detecting counterfeit currency in banks located in border areas, and take appropriate action against suspicious financial transactions as well as fake or dubious bank accounts. Ensure effective action against drug trafficking to curb the movement of narcotics across the border,”Mr. Choudhary said.

The Chief Minister directed that regular monthly coordination meetings should be held between the District Magistrates and police officials of border districts and central security and investigative agencies. He also instructed to identify unregistered religious sites in border areas and take necessary action in accordance with prevailing laws. Bihar CM ordered that better educational facilities in border areas should be made available.

Mr. Choudhary asserted that to ensure effective border security, all concerned agencies must work with vigilance, information sharing, and coordinated action. He added that while strengthening the intelligence network in sensitive areas, ensure prompt and lawful action against any suspicious activity.

District Magistrates (DMs) and Superintendents of Police (SPs) from border districts also joined the meeting through video conferencing.

OpenAI says its AI agents posted user images online in error

Trump says he does not want to ‘integrate’ with China on AI

President Donald Trump said on ​Saturday (September 26, 2026) that despite ‌a “big talk” this week ​with Chinese President Xi ⁠Jinping on AI, the U.S. should not join efforts ‌with China on the technology.

Press Club condemns detention of journalists covering protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

The Press Club of India (PCI), in a statement issued in New Delhi on Saturday (September 26, 2026), condemned the Delhi Police’s decision to detain two journalists, Frontline’s Vedaant Lakhera and The Wire’s Mohammad Irfan, who were covering a protest at Jantar Mantar on Friday against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

It’s not BRICS or UN, BRICS is supportive of UN: Jaishankar

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has said that choosing between groupings such as BRICS and the United Nations is “a false choice”, emphasising that smaller groups are supportive of the global organisation and would like to see it reformed.

TVK government losing trust of Communist parties reflects its failure, says Udhayanidhi Stalin

Leader of the Opposition and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) youth wing leader Udhayanidhi Stalin on Saturday (September 26) sought to impress upon voters in Dharapuram (SC) Assembly Constituency that the decision of Communist parties, with whose support the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) formed the government, to contest in the byelection was a reflection of their disappointment with the ruling establishment’s governance.

China pushes back against U.S. on Iran and Cuba in UN speech

World.title: Congress accuses CEC of law violation over Form 6 changes, urges Supreme Court to hold him accountable
World.content:
The Congress on Saturday (September 26, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of knowingly breaking the law and Constitutional practices by "unilaterally" changing Form 6 and called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable.

In a post on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Mr. Kumar's continued tenure is an affront to the people of India and that he must resign, as suggested by Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.

Mr. Ramesh stated that late at night on Friday (September 25, 2026), a "panicked" Election Commission directed officers to organise special enrolment camps for young voters and give them "wide publicity" through social media.

Also Read: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive

"But the CEC himself had earlier made it virtually impossible to add young voters through a blatantly illegal and unconstitutional change to Form 6. A new mandatory section was added that asks if your parents/grandparents were in the previous SIR, creating a barrier for first-time Gen Z voters.

"The change is completely illegal. -- Violation 1: In early July 2026, the online form was stealthily changed with no official notification," the Congress leader said.

Pointing out the second violation, he said the ECI does not have the power to amend Form 6. "This power is only held by the Union Government as per the Representation Of The People Act, 1950. This is clearly a huge overreach by the Election Commission," Mr. Ramesh said.

"Violation 3: The form was changed without any amendment to the Rules that govern it under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. That can only be done by the Union Government with proper intimation to Parliament. A statutory form, defined by the law, was unilaterally changed by the CEC Gyanesh at the instance of the rattled PM-HM duo," he added.

Mr. Ramesh claimed that, incidentally, the two election commissioners had called for this "illegal and unauthorised" change to be reversed "so young and first-time voters can register without any harassment".

"The CEC has broken not just Constitutional conventions and practices but has also knowingly broken the law as passed by Parliament. His continuation in office is an affront to the people of India.

"A confirmed law-breaker in charge of implementing laws -- what has Indian democracy degenerated into. The Supreme Court must immediately take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable," the Congress general secretary said.

He asserted that Mr. Kumar can still redeem himself by resigning and turning approver, a suggestion by Rahul Gandhi, adding that the youth will approve this move.

Amid a row over the Election Commission adding a declaration to the form for new voters seeking to enrol in the electoral rolls and making the registration process difficult, poll panel officials said on Friday (September 25, 2026) that as many as 2.37 crore electors in the 18- 28-year age bracket were added since the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise was rolled out in Bihar last June.

After the change in the online form, it's not only the existing voters who must show details of their parents in the SIR to remain on the electoral rolls; those seeking inclusion in the voter list also have to cite details of the exercise.

By issuing instructions, the Election Commission has made it mandatory to attach SIR details of parents for new voters filling Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls.

A poll panel functionary underlined that the declaration was added through instructions and that Form 6 has not been amended.

If a person fills out Form 6 online, he or she cannot proceed further till the declaration is filled.

World.title: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive
World.content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday (September 26, 2026) announced a slew of measures addressing concerns over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls across the country, including stopping physical hearings for unmapped voters or those with logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.

It said that the declaration accompanying Form 6 (used for fresh voter registration) is mandatory only during the current SIR process. This in effect means that new voters who seek inclusion in electoral rolls after the ongoing SIR need not submit any such declaration.

The commission also said that any person whose name has got left out during SIR or thereafter, and any person including young/ first-time voters, may apply to the electoral registration officer (ERO) concerned, for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls. A special drive will immediately be launched for their enrolment, it said in a press note.

The SIR process has already been completed in 20 States and Union Territories.

The fresh initiatives of the poll body came after a meeting of the full bench of the commission on Saturday afternoon (September 26, 2026) and days after reports emerged of a rift within the Election Commissioners over these and other issues in the SIR process as well as the internal working of the ECI.

The press note confirmed that the two Commissioners had written to the Cabinet Secretary but said it was not related to any policy matter of the commission or IT division but related to working of an officer on deputation to the ECI. “The work re-distribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not actually implemented after the orders of the two Commissioners,” it clarified.

The commission’s press note was pertinently accompanied by a photograph of all the three Election Commissioners and mentioned that it “has the approval of the full commission”.

As far as physical hearings were concerned, the statement said: “In case of any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and for logical discrepancies, BLOs (booth-level officers) will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO.”

“Such persons need not be called for hearing to ERO/AERO office. Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, the hearing will be held preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required. Facilities for the online hearing are to be strengthened.”

As regards new voter registration, the EC maintained that the declaration form attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court, but for non-SIR period, the forms appFmahalicable as per rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used for new voter inclusion.

Also read | Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar

Access issue

The other issue that had attracted the ire of the two Election Commissioners was the supposed centralisation of management of voter rolls through the ECINet portal, with field officers unable to access it in many cases.

The statement said that “A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission”. It added that henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the commission.

“Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. In case, any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational,” it added.

The commission also extended the period for filing claims and objections for Delhi till October 30 and for Maharashtra till October 12.

Many other administrative measures were also announced. These include circulation of an advanced agenda and issuance of minutes for all of Commission’s meetings, completion of annual performance appraisal reports of all the officers within the stipulated time frame, approval of the commission for foreign trips of officers and compliance with all directions issued by the Commissioners to the officers of the Commission.

The Opposition, which has been seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, remained unimpressed with the statement. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said: “The CEC thinks he can hide behind protocol. He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable.”

“The ongoing SIR which has turned to be method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of India must be suspended immediately without delay. In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC’s resignation or prosecution will suffice”.

World.title: ECI’s ‘unanimous clarification’ on SIR puts to rest all misconceptions: says A.P. CM Naidu
World.content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has stated that the unanimous clarification issued by the Election Commission, led by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alongside Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of India’s constitutional bodies and put to rest all the misconceptions surrounding the process.

The decisions concerning the SIR were taken collectively and in strict adherence to established institutional protocols, Mr. Naidu observed in a social media post on Saturday (September 26, 2026).

Also Read: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive

Mr. Naidu noted that attempts to undermine global confidence in India’s democratic framework or electoral processes for short-term political gain were “deeply unfortunate.”

“Electoral outcomes reflect the people’s mandate and in a robust democracy, leadership also means accepting both victories and defeats with grace and humility,” he commented, adding that it was the collective responsibility of leaders across party lines to uphold public confidence in India’s democratic process.

World.title: Match sickle cell status, not horoscopes before marriage, say experts in Odisha
World.content:
Malini (name changed) from Odisha’s Angul district did not have a conventional arranged marriage. Instead of matching horoscopes with her prospective husband, she and her family relied on the couple’s medical reports before agreeing to the marriage.

Malini, 42, has lived with sickle cell disease (SCD), a genetic disorder affecting red blood cells, since birth. Yet, she went on to have a successful marriage and is now the mother of a healthy 12-year-old son.

Asish, a manager with public-sector Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), was not as fortunate. Despite having a stable and well-paying job, he could not convince his girlfriend’s family that there was no harm in marrying her. Even a renowned haematologist tried to mediate, but the couple’s nine-year relationship eventually failed to culminate in marriage.

Odisha is among the 17 states with a high prevalence of SCD. According to available data, around 10.61% of the population screened in the state has either sickle cell trait (SCT) or sickle cell disease.

Asish, a Homozygous Sickle Cell Anaemia patient, said he could endure the excruciating pain caused by the disease, but found it far more difficult to overcome the stigma associated with it.

“Social stigma affects people with sickle cell disease more than the disease itself,” members of the newly formed National Alliance for Sickle Cell and Thalassemia Control (NASCETC) said at its first meeting held on the sidelines of the 16th annual congress of the Odisha Haematology Association here on Saturday (September 26, 2026). The voluntary forum has been formed to create a stronger support system for people living with SCD and thalassemia.

The Union government launched the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Programme (NSCAEP) on July 1, 2023, across 17 high-prevalence states, including Odisha, with the goal of eliminating SCD as a public health problem by 2047.

“The programme is one of India’s largest initiatives to control a genetic disease and is being closely watched internationally because of its scale and comprehensive community-based approach. Besides medical interventions, we also need to address the taboos and social stigma surrounding the disease. People living with SCD themselves must take the lead in creating awareness about the condition,” said Professor R. K. Jena, a renowned haematologist.

Experts, including Ruby Khan, Deputy Director of the National Health Mission, Madhya Pradesh, and Manoranjan Mohapatra, Head of the Department of Haematology at AIIMS, Delhi, advised patients and their families that people living with sickle cell disease can lead a healthy married life if their partner does not have either sickle cell trait (SCT) or sickle cell disease.

“Kundli milao ya na milao, lekin sickle cell reports milana zaruri hai (Match horoscopes or not, but matching sickle cell medical reports is a must). Pregnant women should also undergo prenatal diagnosis, while screening of family members should be carried out as a preventive measure,” said Dr. Khan.

Prof Mohapatra said that, unlike thalassaemia, people with SCD can lead normal lives and that, not every patient requires a bone marrow transplant.

“Not every patient will require a bone marrow transplant. Patients must follow the advice prescribed by their doctors and overcome their fears,” he said.

Although medicines such as hydroxyurea, which helps reduce the frequency and severity of pain episodes, are available at government hospitals, and haematology departments have been opened at several government and private hospitals, patients and their families continue to face social stigma associated with the disease.

“In Kandhamal district, where we are studying the social stigma attached to blood disorders, we have found that some people collect medicines from places far from their homes to conceal their condition from neighbours. Marriages also take place without families disclosing the medical condition of their sons or daughters,” said Debarpita Mohanty, a scientist at the ICMR’s Regional Medical Research Centre, Bhubaneswar.

World.title: Trump rejects Iran proposal for deal to reopen Hormuz
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Saturday (September 26, 2026) rejected a truce deal proposed by Iran that Tehran said could have reopened the Strait of Hormuz to shipping within a week.

The waterway is key to the world's energy supply and is now central to the conflict between the US and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months.

"I reject their proposal," Mr. Trump told reporters outside the White House. "They made a proposal but I've rejected it."

"They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they're losing so badly. They want to make a deal and I think that's fine. I like making a deal too."

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, who was on his way back to Tehran after attending the UN General Assembly in New York, told CBS News the proposal had been developed "in coordination" with supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, according to an excerpt from the video interview shared by Iranian media.

Iran's plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in West Asia, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who met earlier in the week with Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff.

He said the conditions were the same as those laid out in a memorandum of understanding signed with the U.S. earlier this year, which called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the U.S. naval blockade.

On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz, Mr. Pezeshkian told CBS that the "process will begin from the very day they accept it".

At the UN, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan complained that the "international community has been absent" and failing to live up to the responsibility to keep the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab open.

"The kingdom rejects any party's use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states," he said, stressing the waterways' importance to global energy security.

His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, told member states that "Russia, together with other responsible states, stands ready to constructively contribute to stabilizing this strategically important region."

In New York, Mr. Pezeshkian met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to his office, and said: "Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table but, given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States."

Mr. Araghchi said at the UN: "Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days."

"The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure," he added.

However, within hours of his comments, The Wall Street Journal reported that Mr. Trump was sceptical that Tehran would meet his demands and expects to renew the U.S. bombing campaign.

Mr. Trump also posted an image to his Truth Social platform of a map showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled "Trump Strait".

Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: "We will not cease punishing the U.S. until Iran's seven conditions are met."

Hostilities in Yemen

Mr. Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran's demands.

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, to reopen the strait and to launch talks on Iran's nuclear programme.

But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.

Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.

Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

World.title: IHC voids law allowing agencies to curb travel
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has declared unconstitutional a provision of the Passport Rules, 2021, that allowed the placement of a citizen’s name on the Passport Control List (PCL) on the recommendation of government agencies or departments without identifying a competent authority or providing legal safeguards.

Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Minhas, in a detailed judgement, declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) ultra vires the Passports Act, 1974, and Articles 4, 9, 10A and 15 of the Constitution, holding that it was of no legal effect.

The judgement was issued on a petition filed by Moinuddin, who was offloaded at Islamabad International Airport on Dec 18, 2025, while travelling to Saudi Arabia for Umrah. He possessed a valid Pakistani passport, a valid Saudi visa and a confirmed air ticket, but no reason was communicated to him for stopping him from travelling.

The court noted that his passport had never been impounded, confiscated, cancelled or inactivated, nor had its issuance or renewal been refused. The dispute, therefore, centred on the question whether the agency had the authority to restrain a citizen from travelling on a valid passport.

According to the judgement, his name was placed on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, on the recommendation of NCB-INTERPOL, forwarded by the FIA’s Assistant Director (Immigration Wing). The action followed his deportation from the UK after his conviction for causing death by dangerous driving while under the influence of alcohol. He had served a three-year sentence.

The court noted that he had completed his sentence and been deported, while no criminal case, inquiry or investigation was pending against him in Pakistan. He was neither a proclaimed offender nor the subject of an extradition request.

The IHC rejected the justification provided by the passport authorities to retain his name on the PCL that his conduct had adversely affected Pakistan’s reputation and that the placement was intended to create deterrence.

The court observed that these grounds were not contained in the Passports Act or the Passport Rules. Rule 21 dealt with refusal of a passport and did not authorise restraint of a citizen who already possessed a valid passport, the judgement stated.

“The refusal of a passport and the prohibition of travel are two separate exercises of power,” Justice Minhas observed, declaring that the function of the relevant division and directorate general to “prepare and maintain” the PCL was administrative and did not itself confer jurisdiction to decide whose name could be placed on the list.

The court pointed out that Rule 22(2) referred to individuals whose passport facilities had been refused. Moinuddin had never been refused a passport. It also noted that Rule 22(2)(a) specifically identified the additional secretary of the relevant division as the authority competent to place and remove names in Category A, whereas clause (b) identified no such authority.

The IHC held that neither the directorate general of FIA nor NCB-INTERPOL possessed the authority to place the petitioner’s name on the PCL in the circumstances of the case.

It observed that the impugned order merely stated that it had been issued with the approval of the “competent authority” without identifying that authority, the legal provision invoked or the material on which the decision was based.

The court found that the impugned provision provided no competent authority, objective criteria, notice, hearing, reasons or communication of the decision, meaning that a citizen could learn of the restriction only after being stopped at the immigration counter.

The judgement declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) — allowing PCL placement on the recommendations of government agencies or departments — beyond Sections 8 and 13 of the Passports Act and inconsistent with the Constitution.

About the reasons of “international reputation” and “deterrence”, the court held that since the petitioner had completed his sentence and no proceedings were pending against him, the restraint had no “live and proximate nexus with a present necessity”.

“Gravity does not supply jurisdiction,” it said.

Expressing displeasure over the authorities’ failure to comply with an earlier order, the IHC directed them to decide the petitioner’s application within one week through a speaking and well-reasoned order.

The court consequently set aside the Jan 26, 2026, order of the agency and declared the petitioner’s placement on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

It directed the authorities to remove his name from the PCL within 15 days of receiving a certified copy of the judgement and not to interfere with his lawful foreign travel on the basis of the impugned placement.

The court clarified that the competent authority could still take action warranted by law after following the prescribed procedure. Copies of the judgement were sent to the Interior Secretary, Immigration and Passports DG and FIA DG for compliance.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: Suicide blast targeting DI Khan checkpost claims 12 lives, injures 30
World.content:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: A dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured on Saturday when a vehicle laden with explosives was rammed into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan’s Darazinda tehsil, officials said.

Separately, two rescue workers were killed and another was injured when a Rescue 1122 ambulance came under fire while transporting bodies of victims from the blast.

DI Khan Regional Police Officer (RPO) Ghulam Mubashir Maken, citing an initial assessment, confirmed the casualties from the blast. He clarified that no law enforcement or security personnel were among the deceased, which included a Customs official and civilians.

The deceased comprised nine men, two women and a minor.

According to police and Rescue 1122 officials, an unidentified attacker rammed the explosives-laden tractor trolley into the checkpost. DI Khan District Police Officer (DPO) Ziauddin Ahmed confirmed that it was a suicide blast.

The blast destroyed a large portion of the checkpost and completely demolished a house adjacent to the post. The intensity of the explosion was such that it was heard over a considerable distance, according to local officials and residents. Heavy firing was also heard following the blast.

The Aman Mela checkpost, located near Mughal Kot and Darazinda on the DI Khan-Quetta Road, is used by police for security and checking along the route. It is situated close to the border between Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

According to RPO Maken, 25 of the injured were taken to the district headquarters (DHQ) hospital. Meanwhile, District Excise Officer Faheem Wazir said Excise personnel present at the checkpost remained safe.

A bomb disposal team was also sent to the site to determine the nature of the explosion and examine the scene, police said.

DPO Ahmed and the superintendent of police for the Saddar area had reached the site soon after the explosion and supervised the rescue operation. A Rescue 1122 spokesperson noted that their teams were on the site for relief operations, but mobile phone services were unavailable in the area.

Later in the day, a Rescue 1122 spokesperson said the search, recovery and relief operation at the site had been completed.

More than 25 personnel, six ambulances and a fire vehicle took part in the relief operations, according to the rescue service. On the directions of District Emergency Officer (DEO) Mohammad Arif Khan, four additional ambulances with staff were dispatched from DI Khan to assist in evacuating the injured.

2 killed as ambulance comes under fire

Rescue 1122 said two of its workers were killed while another was seriously injured when an ambulance transporting some bodies recovered from the blast site was targeted by unidentified assailants near Aman Mela.

The deceased rescue workers were identified as Sharifullah and Imtiaz, while Anees sustained injuries in the firing, according to a Rescue 1122 spokesperson.

The injured worker was provided immediate medical treatment and taken to a hospital. Despite the firing incident, rescue teams had continued the operation to transport the bodies and assist those affected by the blast.

State broadcaster Radio Pakistan attributed the attack to Fitna al Khawarij, a term the state uses to refer to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

The report added that an operation by the security forces against the terrorists was underway.

‘Political priorities must reflect the pain of our people’

Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, in a video statement, condemned the attack and highlighted the funds allocated for police in KP’s budget. He also once again called for a “policy shift” on the federal government’s part regarding counterterrorism.

Meanwhile, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi sought a report from senior officials on the incident and directed that every possible medical facility be provided to those injured.

“The attack is a nefarious conspiracy by Fitna al-Hindustan Khawarij,” the governor said.

The state refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

In the wake of the blast, Kundi also requested the PTI to call off its march to Islamabad planned for Oct 4.

Tagging CM Afridi’s X account, he wrote: “For the sake of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and our people, let us put political differences aside and stand together as one.

“Our people are paying the price in blood. They deserve solidarity, security and leadership focused on protecting their lives.”

In an earlier post on X, Kundi said, “At a time when KP is mourning, political priorities must reflect the pain of our people.”

He asserted that the provincial government “must take responsibility and put the security and lives of our people at the centre of its priorities”.

“They do not need test matches or long marches. They need peace.”

Condemnations

President Asif Ali Zardari strongly condemned the blast in a statement issued by the Presidency and expressed grief over the lives lost.

The president ordered that the best medical facilities be provided to the injured, and that relief operations be made “more effective”.

“Making innocent citizens and law enforcement personnel a target of terrorism is highly condemnable,” he was quoted as saying.

“Operations against terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan and Fitna al Khawarij, who perpetrate heinous acts with foreign support, must be made more effective.”

Denouncing the attack, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the loss of precious human lives.

He said the sacrifices of the nation’s guardians in the war against terrorism “will never be allowed to go in vain”. “The government is determined to completely eradicate terrorism from the country,” he was quoted as saying.

In a statement issued by his ministry, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also strongly condemned the “suicide blast at the anti-smuggling Aman Mela police checkpost” and expressed his condolences to the bereaved families.

“The cowardly acts of kharjis cannot weaken the nation’s firm resolve against terrorism,” he was quoted as saying, using a term the state employs to designate terrorists.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is on the front lines of the fight against terrorism.”

Naqvi noted that people from all walks of life have made sacrifices against terrorism, adding that the state deeply values the sacrifices of martyrs.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said that the “terrorist attack” in DI Khan, following the recent bloodshed in Kohat, was “another painful reminder of the terrorism threat Pakistan continues to confront”.

“My deepest condolences to the families of our martyrs and prayers for the injured. The nation stands firmly with our courageous police, law-enforcement agencies and security forces,” he said.

“Pakistan has defeated terrorism before, and we will defeat it again. Terrorists, their facilitators, financiers and sponsors will be held accountable and no territory beyond our borders will be allowed to serve as a sanctuary for terrorism against Pakistan,” he said.

“We will neither be intimidated nor divided. Pakistan will prevail,” Bilawal said.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb also condemned the blast at the “Customs joint check post”.

Rise in terrorism

KP has witnessed an increase in terrorist activity in recent months, with law enforcement agencies and security forces being targeted, prompting authorities to intensify counterterrorism operations.

Earlier this month, police said they foiled an attack by TTP terrorists on a checkpost in DI Khan’s Daraban area. No casualties were reported among the police personnel.

On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation .

In response to that and other terrorist incidents, Pakistan days later conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying over 28 terrorists were eliminated.

Mainland KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks in August compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

World.title: Missiles fired at Riyadh, intercepted by coalition
World.content:
RIYADH: The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles, as the group launched fresh attacks, including on Riyadh, despite international condemnation.

A spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition said on Saturday its air defences “intercepted and destro­yed two drones launched by the Houthis towards the Riyadh area”.

Saudi air defences also intercepted and destroyed two Houthi-launched ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait, a city in the country’s southwest that is home to an air base, the spokesman said.

Hezam Al-Assad, a member of the Houthi Political Bureau, said on Saturday that “Despite the operation’s strength, scope, and impact, our armed forces view it as merely a small-scale rehearsal for a full-scale escalation.”

Meanwhile, Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, secretary general of the Gulf Cooperation Council, denounced the Houthi attacks.

“This dangerous escalation constitutes a flagrant violation of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and poses a direct threat to the security and safety of civilians and the stability of the region,” he said in a statement.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: 'Protest everyone's right but minus Islamabad': Sanaullah says 'practice' of marches to capital should end
World.content:
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah contended on Saturday that everyone had a constitutional and legal right to protest, but Islamabad should be off-limits for demonstrations and urged people to “end the practice” of staging long marches and protests in the federal capital.

PTI had been gearing up for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. However, the party announced a day ago that the march has been postponed to Oct 4.

Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) had also launched a march towards Islamabad against the petroleum levy, but it postponed the move at the request of PM Shehbaz Sharif, pending a meeting with him.

“If anyone needs to protest, they can do so in Faisalabad, Hyderabad, Karachi, Peshawar, or Multan. This practice needs to end,” Sanaullah said on Geo News programme ‘Jirga’.

He pointed out that the ban on protests in Islamabad did not apply only to the PTI. Gatherings in the capital without prior permission are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024 , which had been rushed through the National Assembly ahead of a PTI gathering that month.

“Peaceful protest is everyone’s constitutional and legal right, but they need to minus Islamabad from that,” Sanaullah stated. “It is everyone’s right, but minus attacks on Islamabad. This must be ensured.”

He highlighted that a message had been sent that no protests would be allowed within Islamabad, as foreign diplomats were present in the federal capital and demonstrations would send a “bad message”.

The PML-N leader accused PTI of aiming to overthrow the government, alleging that their goal is to “erect ladders next to the walls of Adiala jail and break in to meet Imran Khan”, who has been incarcerated there since an Aug 5, 2023 conviction.

“How is this peaceful?” Sanaullah asked.

“Party leaders have been threatening to overthrow the government or free someone from jail and then go back,” he outlined. “Permission for a long march will not be granted if this is their intent.”

The PM’s aide stressed that no streets in Islamabad, besides those in the Red Zone and the M-1 Motorway, were shut for traffic. He clarified that containers had only been placed “at the corners” of the city’s roads for “safety”.

“There are containers on every corner of Islamabad, but as we speak right now, no roads have been closed with them,” he said, explaining that containers have been placed at those points so they can be deployed as and when needed.

“The situation in Islamabad is not as it is being described in the media,” he asserted, noting that some were referring to the capital as a “container city”.

The PM’s aide stressed that PTI also did not submit any application to the Islamabad administration seeking permission for a gathering, nor inform it of its expected time and duration.

Sanaullah added that PTI should approach the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and provide their “required guarantees”, contending that they did not intend to do that.

Asked if the authorities’ response to any march would be similar to the Nov 26, 2024 crackdown on PTI’s ’Final Call’ protest, Sanaullah said he did not want to “say any such thing” as there were fellow Pakistanis, friends and colleagues in the party.

However, he warned that PTI “should not hold such a march at any cost that would attempt to push back law enforcement agencies and move towards D-Chowk”.

“Under no circumstance will they be granted access,” Sanaullah warned, cautioning PTI supporters against using force, noting that such an action, in the wake of IHC’s recent ruling, would provide authorities with “legal backing” to respond.

Hearing a plea against the planned march, the IHC on September 14 ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

Meanwhile, in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory, security measures and preparations to deal with any emergency situation remain in place despite the postponement of the march.

Punjab had already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province until Oct 5 and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months.

World.title: Eight terrorists killed in Dera Bugti clash, police claim
World.content:
• Peace force member martyred, three injured; seven ‘terrorists’ arrested

• Tribal leader shot dead in Khuzdar; Bizenjo’s residence attacked

QUETTA/KHUZDAR: At least eight suspected terrorists were killed in a clash with the Bugti Peace Force, a pro-government tribal militia, in the Loti area of Dera Bugti district on Saturday, according to police officials.

A policeman who was part of the peace force was martyred and three other members were injured during the clash.

Separately, a tribal leader was killed in the Naal area of Khuzdar and firing was also reported at the residence of Sardar Aslam Bizenjo, a central leader of the National Party, in the same area.

Police officials said that following the clash, the peace force arrested seven suspected terrorists who allegedly belonged to a banned outfit.

Sources said armed men attacked the residence of Dera Bugti District Council Chairman Ghulam Nabi Shambani and a gas company camp in the Loti area of Dera Bugti district with heavy weapons in the early hours of Saturday.

The Bugti Peace Force personnel, who were deployed for the protection of the district council chairman and the gas company camp, took positions and returned fire.

An exchange of fire continued for over an hour, during which heavy weapons, including rockets, were used by both sides. Some attackers were killed in the exchange of fire.

Sources said that after the heavy exchange of fire, some attackers escaped from the site. However, they returned later in the day and again attacked the residence of the Dera Bugti district council chairman, who is close to Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti.

The sources added that eight attackers were killed in the exchange of fire while seven others were arrested by the peace force. Their bodies were shifted to Loti hospital.
